screening_results.reason: The study reports fMRI activation to dynamic social interaction videos in a sample of 20 young adult volunteers (healthy adults). The task is explicitly social (positive and negative social encounters), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The abstract states whole-brain and hemispheric activation with significant right>left effects (p<0.0001) in multiple regions (amygdaloid complex, IFG, fusiform, temporal gyri), indicating group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results from the healthy sample. There is no indication that results are ROI-only, connectivity-only, or limited to non-adult ages. Full text access is limited, but the abstract provides clear evidence that inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (kinship-based affiliative vs nonaffiliative scenarios) with healthy adult participants (final N=27; ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected results, whole-brain and ROI-corrected contrasts) with tables/figures and coordinates. The full text includes methods, behavioral and imaging results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the article is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study investigating social perception (affiliation vs. isolation) during a task with pleasantness ratings. It includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age 20.75) within the 18–65 range and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM2 results, thresholding, coordinate tables, conjunction analyses, and figures) for the healthy groups. Results for younger (healthy) and older groups are reported separately and whole-brain task-evoked effects (e.g., temporal pole, medial PFC, precuneus, hippocampus) are presented in tables/figures. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and provides the necessary group-level whole-brain activation maps/statistics in the main text/tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI during a social-related task (affiliation and power movie clips) in healthy adult participants (n=17 males, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (affiliation > control; power > control) and regression analyses with activation clusters and MNI coordinates presented in Table 1 and Figure 2. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are applicable.

This is an empirical fMRI study directly investigating social-context vs. non-social episodic memory (social interaction / social scripts) using a task that manipulates social vs. solitary conditions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24, ages 18–28). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM5, voxelwise contrasts, thresholding, cluster correction) with tables/figures of activations. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 26) that used a social-related task (observation of social vs. individual actions with gaze manipulation). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, voxelwise contrasts (main effects and interaction) with SPM maps and coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The paper therefore meets the review’s criteria for fMRI social-processing tasks in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are triggered.

This study is an fMRI experiment investigating social interaction and self-involvement using virtual characters (social communication and perception of self/others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (18 right-handed males, mean age 25.9; analyses reported for n=17), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported stereotactic coordinates, tables and figures of main effects and interactions (e.g., SOC>ARB, ME>OTHER), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines understanding of others' regret (a social-related ‘perception and understanding of others’ task) using task-based BOLD fMRI. Participants are healthy adults (two samples of 24 each; ages reported within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., IP minus IF and OP minus OF), parametric and conjunction analyses, and reports activation foci/coordinates and whole-brain statistical maps described in the text and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and acquisition/analysis details).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract indicates this is an fMRI study of prosodic categorisation relevant to social communication (meets I3). However, the available text does not confirm key required details: participant sample characteristics and age range (I4) are not reported in the abstract, and it is not possible to verify that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5/I6). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included based on the available information. No exclusion criteria E2–E6 are explicitly met from the abstract alone.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affiliative emotion (tenderness/affection) vs pride using task-based fMRI with multivariate and univariate analyses. Sample: healthy adult participants (mean age 24.5) are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses in SPM8 and provides voxel coordinates, cluster sizes and statistics (MNI coordinates and Z-values) for effects (even though FWE-corrected significance was obtained via Small Volume Correction). Whole-brain preprocessing and voxelwise analyses are described and whole-brain results (with statement that none survived whole-brain FWE) are reported, and coordinates/figures of activation are given. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: It uses task-based fMRI with social-related stimuli (pictures of faces as target events) within an oddball target-detection paradigm, addressing social processing. I4: The sample comprises healthy adults (N=19; age range 19.3–47.5), with screening for psychiatric symptoms and separate reporting of this (healthy) group. I5/I6: The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (shape targets–novels, face targets–novels, and direct comparisons) analyzed with FSL (cluster-corrected Z and P thresholds), and presents figures and a table of MNI coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper reports original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (live social interaction and joint attention tasks) in healthy adults (participants aged 18–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with corrected statistics and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using social-cognition tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) meeting the review objective. The sample includes a healthy control group of adults (n=13) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain group-level activations and single-group results (reported at P<0.001 uncorrected; single-group results noted in Supplementary Tables S1–S4), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are adults, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study in a healthy adult sample (24 males, ages 19–60) using a deception task that probes social-cognitive processes (deception, theory-of-mind/mentalising and manipulation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (lie > truth and truth > lie) with statistical maps/tables and cluster coordinates, and applies small-volume corrections; results for the healthy/control group are reported directly. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing (empathy/theory-of-mind) in healthy adults (N=16 analyzed; mean age 27.8), using a social task (viewing emotional vs. neutral social scenes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (EMOT vs NEUT; TWO vs ONE) with Talairach coordinates, tables, figures and voxelwise statistical maps (FDR q<0.05) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Results are not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or patient-group-only contrasts. Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain healthy adult fMRI social processing studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study that implemented an interactive, social gaze-based task (joint and non-joint attention) during whole-brain fMRI acquisition in healthy adult participants (n=24; age range 20–34), satisfying the sample requirement. Group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self > other; JA > NJA) are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics from second-level analyses (reported in text/figures), meeting the whole-brain results criterion. Although many inferences used small-volume correction for a priori ROIs, group-level voxelwise contrasts for the healthy sample are explicitly reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (images of social group interactions vs individuals) while participants imagined themselves in the situations. A healthy control group (n=29; adults ≈32 years) is reported separately and reported within-group (control) whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., group-positive vs group-neutral; group-negative vs group-neutral) with voxelwise coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results (control group main effects and contrasts), figures, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-processing study in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps/coordinates for the healthy/control group.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of facial emotion processing (a social cognition task: perception/understanding of others' emotions) with a healthy adult control group. Healthy controls are adults (mean age 27±5) within the 18–65 range and their results are reported separately. The paper describes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and presents group activation maps/tables for the control group (contrasts such as neutral vs fixation and emotion vs fixation; methods describe whole-brain permutation-based voxel and cluster thresholding), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group without healthy-group effect, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study uses a social facial-emotion task (I3) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I4). However, the paper reports only between-group (VCFS vs controls) whole-brain contrasts (Table 1 and text) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus I6 is not satisfied for a healthy-group map). Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) passively viewed realistic social interaction video clips (a social-related task). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (corrected P ≤ 0.05 across the whole brain) with figures and tables of activations (including coordinates and clusters), and contrasts versus rest and versus an ‘alone’ condition. These satisfy the review’s requirements for social task fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply.

The study is an fMRI experiment involving social communication tasks (viewing, imitating, and producing facial expressions and social hand gestures), indicating social-related processing (I3). The text describes participants (healthy adult participants rather than clinical groups), meeting the sample requirement (I4). The paper reports neural activation locations and condition differences (e.g., IPL and frontal operculum activations and significant differences in locations), indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported (I5). Results are clearly described in the text, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, resting-state only, non-empirical) are evident from the provided information.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an ecological social-related task (listening to film excerpts and inferring characters’ mental states), including a healthy adult group (HC-S1, n=28; ages 18–65). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy control group (INT>HIN contrast; one-sample t-test, p<0.05 FWE) with tables and figures of activation peaks and maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy group are clearly separable from the patient group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of positive social stimuli: social interactions, human faces, erotic scenes) meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, mean age 28.2) reported separately from the clinical (depressed) group. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise (repeated-measures ANOVAs), and results are reported as cluster tables and figures with coordinates and cluster volumes (Tables 3–5, Figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study meets inclusion criteria I3 (task is a social-related dyadic conversation involving perception/understanding of others) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=14, ages within 18–65). However, the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain results are for combined groups and for between-group contrasts/interactions; ROI extractions and parameter estimates for the control group are provided, but no standalone healthy-group whole-brain statistical map (one-sample/group-level map) is clearly presented. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study in healthy adults (N=44, mean age 22.37) using a social interaction task (pattern game) that manipulates cooperation/competition and concurrent/turn-based interaction—clearly a social-related task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with non-parametric permutation correction and presents cluster coordinates and figures (Tables 1–3, Fig. 4), satisfying whole-brain reporting (coordinates/figures). All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample reported; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI probing social processing (Dynamic Social Gesture task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, face-visibility); (I4) Reports a sample of healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 21.41, range includes adults within 18–65); (I5) Presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (TFCE with permutation testing, reported in figures/tables and text); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (valuation/generation of others’ emotional facial expressions), involving 14 healthy adult participants (mean age ~29, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 with thresholds and reports activated regions and coordinates (whole-brain task contrasts). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Provided ‘‘full text’’ is a 404/error webpage from Frontiers and lacks the core article content (no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion). Therefore it is impossible to confirm whether the study used task fMRI of social processing (I3), included a healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), or reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps from healthy participants (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria from the review (E2–E6) can be assessed as met given the missing content. As a result, the study is excluded due to incomplete full text preventing application of inclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), the paper reports primarily ROI (small-volume corrected) task results and does not present an unmasked, whole‑brain group-level voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group. The authors state they ran whole-brain ANOVAs but constrained inference with ROI masks and report ROI peak coordinates and SVC results (Tables 1–2). There is only a brief mention of an exploratory whole-brain finding (early visual areas) without full coordinates/tables for an unmasked group map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole‑brain group map not provided). Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation), meeting the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (23 right-handed females, age 18–30). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts are reported (e.g., imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with correction for multiple comparisons (FWE p<0.05) and coordinates/tables provided. The study therefore provides whole-brain evidence for the healthy group rather than only ROI or connectivity-only results (although PPI is also reported). All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical NeuroImage study uses task-based fMRI (EmpaToM) to probe social affect and social cognition (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises a healthy adult group (N=122; age range 18–57) with analyses reported for the healthy participants. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (second-level flexible factorial models, FWE-corrected thresholding for main contrasts and exploratory whole-brain analyses with reported clusters) and describes whole-brain results in the text and supplementary materials. Thus, it satisfies I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary/materials availability).

This is a task-based fMRI hyperscanning study of joint attention and mutual gaze (social interaction, social communication/perception). Participants: healthy adult volunteers (ages reported, n provided). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of coordinates, cluster-level FWE-corrected results, figures) clearly from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and tables. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Cyberball (virtual ball-toss) social interaction task (social reward/affiliation), with healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages ~21) and explicit reporting of group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates in text/tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (ultimatum game) in healthy adult participants (10 male volunteers, ages 23–28). The paper reports whole-brain offline analyses across subjects (leave-one-subject-out cross-subject SVM) and lists discriminating volumes with MNI coordinates and thresholding (Tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and clearly reports results for the healthy control group. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain evidence reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described).

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining self/other processing (social cognition) using a semantic self/other/letter judgment paradigm, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper includes a healthy typically-developing (TD) control group and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps and tables for the TD group (e.g., self vs. letter contrasts shown in figures and Table 2). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described in the text, figures, and tables. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Although the sample description includes some participants under 18 in the initial recruitment, the study reports separate healthy-group whole-brain task effects; this satisfies the requirement for a healthy adult control group for inclusion in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This article reports an event-related fMRI study of social interaction (SI) recognition (a social-related task) using point-light displays (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult group (N=16, ages 20–41) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SI > NM) for the adult group using SPM8 with peak- and cluster-level thresholding and FWE corrections; activations for adults (e.g., bilateral pMTG/pSTS, IFG, dmPFC, caudate) are explicitly described (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, adult group within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (valence judgments of naturalistic social interactions) in a healthy adult sample (N=38, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Social > Non-social contrasts; full-factorial ANOVA) with FWE correction and provides activation tables/figures and coordinates. Results are for the healthy/control group (no clinical subgroup only reporting). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (face learning via real-world social interactions). fMRI was used during a task involving perception of faces (social perception/understanding of others), meeting I3. Participants were healthy adults (n=22, age 18–35), meeting I4. The authors report a whole-brain group-level analysis (two-way mixed ANOVA across all 22 healthy participants) and note whole-brain results (subthreshold clusters) included in the online Supplemental Materials, fulfilling I5 and I6 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported in supplemental material and clearly from the healthy group). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), ages are within range (E5), and it is empirical (E6). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=46; analyzed groups n=18,21) examining effects of social interaction (live signer vs DVD) on neural processing of Japanese Sign Language. The fMRI task involves sign-language comprehension (a form of social communication) and the paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts with coordinates and figures (thresholds and tables provided). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task: social communication via sign language/learning), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based BOLD fMRI collected while healthy adult participants (age 18–22) performed a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (thresholded Z maps and cluster-corrected results reported across sexes and genotypes), with results clearly coming from the healthy sample (OT vs placebo groups). Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and discussed in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is an empirical fMRI study).

The study reports an fMRI task examining social interaction processing (affective and cooperative interactions), satisfying the review’s social-related construct (I3). Sample consists of 36 healthy adult participants (ages ~24–25), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects group analysis; results thresholded and reported with cluster FDR p<.05; tables and figures of activations), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using a task contrasting social interactions (SI) versus non-social interactions (NSI) depicted with point-light displays, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses for the SI-NSI contrast with FDR-corrected results and lists peak voxels/clusters (Table 1; figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (naturalistic movie viewing that elicits social cognition and social interaction processing), includes a healthy adult sample (n=34, mean age 22.2), and reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation results with corrected statistics and visualization (whole-brain χ2 tests, Bonferroni correction; Figure 3). Group-level healthy-participant effects are clearly described. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of understanding others' mental states (false-belief/theory-of-mind task), which is a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (n=34; ages 20–28) with no psychiatric/neurological history. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (ROMS vs. CTRL) with statistical maps, coordinate tables, and ROI analyses supplementing whole-brain results. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults with whole-brain group results). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (implicit/explicit detection of eye-gaze and self-propelling motion; implicit mental-state inference task), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., E–O, S–X; PCA-based regressions) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI tasks; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using point-light dyadic displays and an orthogonal task, meeting the review's construct. Sample: healthy adult participants (ten right-handed males, ages 22–32) are reported separately — satisfies the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts ((atypical upright + atypical inverted) − (typical upright + typical inverted)) with cluster-size correction and tables/figures of activated loci, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/perspective-taking (perception and understanding of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=23, ages 19–34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects contrasts such as Pain > No Pain and target-specific contrasts) with reported statistical thresholds, tables/figures of activation clusters, and PPI connectivity results. Behavioral and dispositional measures for the healthy sample are reported separately. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (gaze/joint attention) in healthy adults. It uses task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; within-subjects ANOVA; voxelwise t-statistics; multiple contrasts reported, tables of activated loci). Sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (behavioral N=10, fMRI N=12), ages 18–40, satisfying the adult age range. Reported whole-brain task activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., gaze shift − no movement; incorrect − correct; social − unsocial) meet the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and figures/tables summary, so appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiments 1 and 2; mean ages ~20–21, within 18–65) that uses a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) contrasted with a non-social control (Gamble), directly addressing social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and random-effects contrasts (e.g., PD–Gamble) with thresholding and tables of activations (Figures/Tables and coordinate lists), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are presented (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This paper reports two fMRI experiments investigating understanding of intentions in social interaction, demonstrating anterior paracingulate cortex activation. The study addresses social-related processing (theory of mind/social interaction) using task-based fMRI in human participants and reports group-level activation (anterior PCC) consistent with whole-brain task effects. It was published in Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience (2004) and presents empirical fMRI results rather than a review. Therefore it meets the review objective and the inclusion criteria for fMRI social tasks, healthy adult sample reporting, and whole-brain results (reported as activation in anterior PCC). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply based on the available full-text abstract and bibliographic information.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related face encoding task (I3), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for the typically-developing control group (I5, I6). However, it is unclear whether the healthy control group consists solely of adults aged 18–65. The methods describe adolescent consent and mock scanning for participants under 18 and provide a mean control age of 18.7 (SD=5.8), indicating that some control participants were likely minors. Inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult group 18–65) is therefore not clearly satisfied based on the provided full text; because at least one inclusion criterion is not met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using a social-related task (trustworthiness judgments of faces) satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=18, mean age 32.2) reported separately from the clinical XXY group, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain task activation analyses for the control group (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures described), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 participants, ages ~35) that used a social-related task (viewing faces of political candidates) addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (FLAME), thresholding and cluster-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, and figures showing task effects and group contrasts. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze-following (a social-related task examining responses to in-group vs. out-group political faces), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 18–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent) with cluster-level correction and provides tables and figures describing activated clusters across the brain (dorsal and ventral fronto-parietal networks, FEF, parietal, occipital regions). Results are reported for the healthy/control sample (no clinical groups). Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an event-related fMRI task that probes social communication (feeling addressed via gesture and body orientation), includes a healthy control group with separate within-group analyses and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation results (conjunctions and group-specific contrasts) with cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables. Although the provided excerpt does not explicitly state participant ages in the text shown, the sample description (healthy subjects recruited, n=48) and standard adult clinical MDD recruitment imply adult participants; confidence is slightly reduced for the absence of an explicit 18–65 age range in the excerpt.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social-related processing (attachment/mentalizing) using task-based fMRI. It reports data from a healthy adult sample (N=25, age range 19–26) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (attachment vs. neutral), including MNI coordinates, cluster sizes, and cluster-level corrected p-values, plus activation maps in figures. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (theory of mind and empathy cartoon task), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=13, ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts analyzed with SPM2 (random-effects) and presents significant activation foci (thresholds, clusters, and tables/figures). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level results.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy comic-strip task) in a healthy sample. Participants are healthy young adults (ages 17–21, mean 19.3) recruited from university; the sample constitutes a healthy adult group within the 18–65 range (majority aged ≥18). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain within-group contrasts (one-sample t-tests and conjunction analyses) with cluster-level inference and tables/figures of activations, and extracts percentage signal change for ROI correlations. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and reporting of whole-brain group-level task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49) that used movie stimuli depicting social/emotional interactions to probe perception/understanding of others and empathy, satisfying social-related task criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise intersubject correlation (ISC) maps and ISC-by-valence/arousal GLM maps with voxelwise FDR-corrected statistics (figures and supplemental tables), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a virtual-reality social cognition task that engages emotional and cognitive aspects of social processing (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (14 right-handed adults, age 18–45) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts for the healthy control group (within-group Emotion vs Control and other contrasts), with coordinates and tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and within-group healthy maps are provided. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (a social-related ToM task), conducted in healthy adult participants (18 right-handed males, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level task-evoked contrasts within the healthy/control group (ToM > gender in the placebo condition) and additionally reports exploratory whole-brain analyses (coordinate tables and figures) comparing LPS vs placebo, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during a faces-versus-houses task (socially relevant face perception), in a healthy adult sample (N=57 total; fMRI subset N=22; mean age ~18.9). The authors performed group-level, whole-brain second-level GLM analyses and report significant whole-brain activations and clusters (bilateral fusiform gyrus; suprathreshold voxel counts and cluster tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group voxelwise task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, pediatric-only, or non-empirical) are violated.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social communication), i.e., a social-related task (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=17, right-handed males, mean age 25.9) meeting the 18–65 criterion (I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FIR model in SPM5) are reported with statistical parametric maps and MNI coordinates (random-effects inference; p=.001 uncorrected, extent threshold), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5,I6). The study is empirical and not ROI- or connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group task activations directly, so it meets inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly manipulates social cognitive load (social working memory task) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric effects with coordinates and figures). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=16; mean age 20) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain results for the healthy group are reported and linked to trait measures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 21–32) that investigates personal prayer vs controls as a social-cognitive task. The contrasts probe theory-of-mind/social cognition (e.g., Personal Praying > Wishes to Santa; Personal Praying > Lord’s Prayer). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates, thresholded at p<0.05 FDR, with MNI/Talairach coordinates and figures). The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group activation maps/coordinates.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI during a social/competitive matching-pennies paradigm involving human and non-human agents (social-related processing/mentalizing). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholding (p<.001) and cluster-level FWE correction across the whole brain; results are presented in figures and tables with coordinates. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (task-based fMRI of social processing, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and appropriately reported maps/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI using social stimuli (traffic awareness videos eliciting socio-cognitive processing), includes healthy adult participants (two groups of right-handed male drivers, ages 19–30), and presents group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) with whole-brain analyses reported for each group and in the text/figures. Thus it meets social-related fMRI task requirement, healthy adult sample, and the presence of whole-brain group-level activation maps/results (reported in figures and text).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (Domino competitive game) engaging social cognition and reward (meets I3). It includes a healthy control group (TD) with participants aged up to 23, thus containing adults in the 18–65 range and reporting their results (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts for the control group (e.g., TD gains>losses and Show>No-Show effects with t-values and corrected clusters), and provides coordinate/cluster-level results and figures (meets I5 and I6). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) appear to apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (men aged 18–22) that used a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) during BOLD fMRI, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Z statistic images, voxel-wise thresholds, FWE cluster-corrected results), with coordinates and cluster sizes described for correlations between Neuroticism and BOLD responses as well as drug interactions, meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; healthy adult group reported; empirical data present).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using a social-comparison task (Close Other vs Non-Close Other) performed in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 18.7). The paper reports group-level, random-effects second-level voxelwise contrasts (SPM{t} maps) and provides peak coordinates and statistical values for task-evoked activations (reported in text and figures/tables). Whole-group healthy participant results are clearly presented (e.g., Target × Breadth and Valence contrasts), meeting the review objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults. Although multiple-comparison correction was implemented within a priori ROIs, the study presents voxelwise, group-level activation maps and coordinate tables for the healthy/control sample.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social working memory (trait-based ranking) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts of parametric modulation by load), thresholding and tables/figures of clusters/coordinates, and links neural activation to behavioral measures of perspective-taking. All required core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining mind perception (a social-cognitive process) using event-related fMRI during a mind-perception task and a separate behavioral gaze-cueing task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 24.4), meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results and peak coordinates (e.g., significant vmPFC clusters) and figures/tables describing these maps. Thus it provides healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps in formats acceptable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a social neuroeconomic paradigm (prisoners' dilemma) addressing social cognition/behavior (trust, cooperation), includes a healthy adult control group (15 controls, ages 18–50) with results reported separately, and presents whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses for controls (within-group one-sample t-tests and group-specific voxelwise results, thresholded and described). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition, paradigm), Results (voxel-based whole-brain analyses for controls and combined groups, ROI and correlations), and Discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, within-age-range, empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-content valence classification task (agency vs. communion), satisfying the review’s focus on social-related processing. Sample: 42 healthy adult participants (ages 18–25), meeting the adult healthy sample requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 with AlphaSim correction; conjunction and contrast maps (agency vs. fixation, communion vs. fixation, and direct contrasts) are reported and described (tables/figures of coordinates referenced). Thus the study provides qualifying whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore I include the study.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social perception task (gender judgments to faces with direct vs averted gaze) addressing perception/understanding of others, with healthy adult participants drawn from the general male population. The fMRI results report group-level task-evoked activation differences (reduced activation in amygdala, fusiform gyrus, anterior superior temporal cortices for low vs normal fear scorers) and functional connectivity findings; these are presented as voxelwise activation contrasts between healthy groups, consistent with whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are evident from the provided full text. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation reported), and I6 (results acceptable as figures/tables).

This study used task-based fMRI of social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=22) reported separately and matched to patients. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task effects (ToM > Emotion > Neutral) with tables of cluster coordinates and statistics, and the manuscript and supplementary materials describe group-specific and within-group contrasts (supplementary analyses are referenced). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (main text and supplementary), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task maps. The full article text including introduction, methods, results and discussion is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Note: some group-specific contrasts are reported in supplementary materials referenced in the text; these are acceptable per I6.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using social-related tasks (emotion processing and theory-of-mind) (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately (meets I4). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects task contrasts and statistical maps for the healthy/control group are described and presented (figures and supplementary tables) using an appropriate voxelwise threshold (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity or resting-state, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects (not only between-group contrasts), includes adults in the target age range, and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making using a modified Ultimatum Game with online verbal negotiations (a social-interaction task). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (male, ages ~18) with group-level analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (random-effects GLM during offer periods; voxelwise threshold and cluster correction described) and provides tables/ supplementary materials with coordinates. Task activation maps and contrasts for the healthy participant group are clearly described (vmPFC, insula, brainstem findings), and PPI connectivity analyses are reported in addition to whole-brain activation. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study used task-based fMRI probing social interaction (a social interaction simulation manipulating relationship type and valence), included a healthy adult sample (28 right-handed participants, age range 19–27), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects; FWE- and cluster-corrected results, figures and Table 1 listing significant clusters). Healthy-group effects (main effects and interactions) are clearly described and reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, clinical-only samples) apply.

This fMRI study examines face emotion discrimination, a social-cognition task (social perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (two community groups screened with SCID; ages consistent with adult university/community sample). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests of EE vs baseline and EE vs EI across all participants, flexible factorial group analyses) with tables of clusters/coordinates and thresholding details. Results for the healthy groups are reported separately (one-sample maps and group comparisons). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (15 healthy males, mean age 26.7). The task involves social-related processing (matching fearful/angry faces) and shows group-level task-evoked activation maps (fearful vs control) for the healthy/placebo condition, reported in figures and analyzed with second-level random-effects models; whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (with ROI-based correction for the amygdala) and results are presented in text, tables, and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from healthy group), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion reason: E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — trustworthiness judgments) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–35, with results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported). The Methods and Results describe voxelwise preprocessing but all inferential results are presented as ROI-based percent signal change and ROI-based statistics; there are no whole-brain, unmasked healthy-group activation maps, coordinate tables, or figures reported for the control group. Therefore the study must be excluded per E2.

This empirical fMRI study acquired whole-brain functional data while healthy adult participants (N=23; ages 19–32) read a literary narrative and provided trial-by-trial suspense ratings. The task elicited activation in theory-of-mind/mentalizing areas (medial frontal cortex, temporo-parietal junction) and predictive-inference regions, i.e., constructs clearly relevant to ‘perception and understanding of others’ (social-related processing). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM; cluster-level FWE correction), and activation tables/coordinates are provided; region-of-interest analyses were supplementary. Thus the paper meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI to probe social/affiliative processing (mothers viewing own vs. unfamiliar child and dog images) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult women aged 22–45 with exclusions for psychiatric or major medical conditions, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., own child vs. fixation, own dog vs. fixation, own child vs. own dog, own vs. unfamiliar) with cluster coordinates, t-values, and activation maps described in the text and figures, providing whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy group (I5,I6). Although analyses used ROI masks and small-volume correction for a priori regions, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts and coordinates are reported rather than only ROI-summary statistics, so the study is not limited by exclusion E2. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Social Context Decision Task (SCDT) that explicitly manipulates social decision-making (peers present) and tests Theory of Mind/self-reflection processes. The sample includes a healthy young adult group (N=30; ages 21–22), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Risk > Ambiguity; Dangerous > Safe) with cluster results, FWE correction, and ROI/FIR follow-ups; cluster coordinates and statistics are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps for healthy adults). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Multifaceted Empathy Test) that probes cognitive and emotional empathy (I3). The sample includes healthy adult control groups (female, age-matched, N≈29–30) reported separately from the BPD patients (I4). The manuscript provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation results for the control/healthy group (tables of activations, coordinates, and main-effect maps/descriptions), using standard GLM mixed-effects analyses and reporting thresholds (I5). Results are reported in-text and in tables/figures (coordinates), satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reporting, or non-empirical design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines social-cognitive processing during observation of toolmaking: participants performed tasks that require simulation (‘Imagine’) and judgement of the demonstrator’s success (‘Evaluate’), tapping perception/understanding of others and intentions. The sample comprises healthy adult groups (Naïve n=11, Trained n=10, Expert n=5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (e.g. Toolmaking–Control; Acheulean–Oldowan) with FDR-corrected thresholds, presented in text, figures and tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a social judgment task (dominance/trustworthiness of faces) in healthy adults (N=23, ages 21–43). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and provides voxelwise results with a table of peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results for the Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment contrast. Results for the healthy adult group are clearly reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports functional MRI during a social cognition task in which participants repeatedly inferred others’ emotions and received feedback—clearly a social-related task. The abstract indicates participants were scanned (perceivers) and no clinical/special groups are mentioned, implying a healthy adult sample. The paper reports trial-by-trial learning signals that tracked activity in ventral striatum, ventromedial PFC, and TPJ, which indicates voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results were analyzed and reported. Reporting in J Cogn Neurosci further supports standard whole-brain analyses. Although the abstract does not state exact ages, the sample is described as typical adult perceivers with no clinical exclusion; thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This empirical fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing using two social-cognitive tasks (Reading the Mind in the Eyes / EToM and basic emotion task / BET), fulfilling task relevance. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14) reported separately from clinical groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses for each group (controls, patients, siblings) with results described in the Whole brain regression section and specific regions listed, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly identified (regions correlating with TABS/SSPA and laterality indices). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social attention (gaze following vs. finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level contrasts and cluster-corrected activations), figures of whole-brain activation patterns and ROI analysis; results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study of social cognition (empathy) using dynamic multimodal social stimuli (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, mean age ~35) with results reported separately (satisfies I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects GLM, cluster-corrected thresholds) and within-group T-contrasts for each participant group, with whole-brain results presented in figures/tables (satisfies I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

The study reports an fMRI social task (anticipation of touching an animate vs inanimate target), uses healthy adult participants (ages 21–33), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results (paired-sample t-tests and FDR-corrected statistical maps and coordinates) clearly from the healthy sample. Whole-brain analyses with covariates (narcissism) are also reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, no between-group-only contrasts, age in range, empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (race perception/trustworthiness), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Black>White) and second-level covariate analyses with tables and peak coordinates, and describes PPI connectivity alongside whole-brain results. Thus it meets criteria for a social-related fMRI task, appropriate healthy adult sample, and provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (reported with coordinates).

This is an empirical fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social decision-making task involving empathy and perspective-taking), with healthy adult participants (N=22; ages 19–38). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (second-level one-sample t tests, whole-brain corrections, coordinates, figures, and supplemental tables). Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain results for healthy group), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (impression formation about people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18.3–23.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trials) with thresholding (P<0.001) and tables/coordinates for peak activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are reported for the healthy sample (no clinical group confound). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates.

This is an fMRI study of social-affective processing (mimicry, affiliation/appeasement) in healthy adults using a task manipulating emotion and group membership, satisfying the review topic. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=41 for fMRI analyses; ages reported, within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts are reported (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent and masked contrasts for Happy vs Angry, Out-group vs In-group) with cluster-level correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4) and detailed methods for SPM analysis. Results are reported for the healthy/control group (no exclusive patient group). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical limitations).

This is an empirical fMRI study of a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm with angry vs neutral opponent videos) in healthy adults. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (31 included in analyses; mean age 23.3), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain results: GLM contrasts (angry > neutral) described in the Results and ICA-derived whole-brain spatial component maps thresholded at z>3.0, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps; results are presented in the main text and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathic concern for characters in film clips) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 30.3), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and contrasts, Tables 1–2, and whole-brain figures) and parametric modulation results for the healthy group, which meet the whole-brain evidence criterion; results are presented in text, tables, and figures. The study additionally includes connectivity (DCM), but also reports univariate whole-brain activations, so it does not violate exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task using social vs. non-social pictures) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported). However it does NOT provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (intra-group healthy results are reported via ROI analyses; whole-brain results are reported only for between-group contrasts as exploratory uncorrected maps). Therefore it fails I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map) and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain healthy results in tables/figures for the healthy group). This matches exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interaction whole-brain results without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion sections, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adult participants (ages 21–38). The task is a social-related, interactive game probing theory-of-mind and social processing (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range and reports group-level analyses for the healthy participants (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts and corrected voxelwise analyses (e.g., active>passive contrasts; meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (approachability and intelligence judgements) in healthy adult participants. A healthy control group (n=47; ages within 18–65) is analyzed and reported separately; a second experiment reports healthy male controls and ASD males separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (social vs gender) are reported using SPM2 with thresholding and cluster correction, with coordinates and figures described in the text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results provided as coordinates/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a social-feedback (acceptance/rejection) task during task-based fMRI (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (20 females, mean age 28.15) and reports controls separately alongside patients (satisfies I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps/analyses for the healthy control group (SPM8 whole-brain analyses with cluster correction; within-group activations for controls are described and shown), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group healthy whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The Domino task is an interactive, competitive game presented as having a human opponent, satisfying the social-related task requirement (I3). The sample comprises 69 healthy participants (FHP and FHN groups) recruited and screened as adults, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses: a random-effects one-sample t-map (n=69) for the Reward-Punishment contrast was used to create a study-specific reward network mask, thresholded at p<0.05 FWE whole-brain corrected and displayed (figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5/I6). Results include voxelwise corrected maps and figures of the reward network and regression analyses within that mask. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, and a healthy-group whole-brain task effect is reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an ecologically valid social interaction task (adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm) presenting opponents' facial expressions; sample comprises healthy adult males (32 included in analyses, mean age 23.3); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and presents tables/figures of whole-brain results. Thus it satisfies fMRI social processing, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three experiments, N=25, N=65, N=178; Experiment 2 mean age 40.9) using a social cognition paradigm (EmpaToM) probing empathy and Theory of Mind, addressing social-related processing. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., empathy contrast, ToM contrast) with tables of activation peaks and figures; second-level one-sample t-tests and FWE-corrected thresholds are described. Behavioral and imaging results for the healthy/control samples are reported separately. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (feeling addressed) that meets all inclusion criteria. It reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (participants judged whether they felt addressed) (I3). The sample comprises 37 healthy adult participants aged 20–39 (I4).
