Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (SPM8), with cluster-corrected results and peak MNI coordinates for main effects and interactions (I5). Results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates (I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=24, ages 20–40) using a social influence task during task-based fMRI and reporting group-level task contrasts (e.g., HC>LC, LC>NC) for the placebo/healthy condition. Whole-group, voxelwise contrasts are described (coordinates and maps/figures reported), and results are presented in text/tables/figures (with both SVC-corrected ROI results and whole-brain uncorrected displays). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task studies in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a naturalistic social stimulus (full-length movie depicting social interactions), meeting the review’s definition of a social-related task. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult (neurotypical) group (n=13, ages 19–47) analyzed separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise intersubject correlation (ISC) maps computed separately for the NT group (and ASD group), with anatomical labels, statistical tests, and MNI coordinates; it also reports NT within-group associations (e.g., AQ correlations) and describes permutation-corrected whole-brain results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not limited to between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, age range appropriate, and empirical). Therefore it should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social-related task (biological motion perception tied to social cognition/ToM), meeting I3. The paper reports a healthy control group (n=17) analyzed and reported separately from the patient group, meeting I4. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (BM–SM, BM–ST) with statistical thresholds and reported activated regions, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI investigation of social-related processing (intimacy, empathy, perspective taking toward Self/Loved-one/Stranger). Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (Pain vs Neutral contrasts across perspectives) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates (FDR-corrected maps and coordinate tables/supplementary tables). Whole-brain correlation and PPI analyses are reported but do not preclude whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (a social cognition task) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 22–56). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy group (within-group ToM vs. random-motion contrast), with corrected voxelwise findings presented in tables and figures. All applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult participants with separate reporting; I5: whole-brain group-level task maps reported; I6: results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social processing in adults and includes a healthy/control (NT) group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain (searchlight) results are reported across all participants combined, and the paper's detailed healthy-group results are ROI-based (not whole-brain). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults using naturalistic audiovisual stimuli. Nineteen healthy adult participants (ages 21–34) viewed movie clips while whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses were performed and reported (FDR-corrected statistical maps, figures, and MNI coordinates in Table 1). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for social vs. non-social features and feature-specific activations. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria are met. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, tables, and appendix) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (audiovisual integration of nonverbal emotional signals), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26.6). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise task contrasts (conjunction (AV > A) AND (AV > V)), voxelwise correlation analyses, coordinate tables and figures (i.e., whole-brain/voxelwise results clearly attributed to the healthy group). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment on socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) involving a psychotherapist regulating participants’ emotions—clearly a social-related task (Affiliation/Attachment; social cognition). The sample comprises healthy adults (22 females, ages 22–32) with group-level analyses reported for the healthy participants. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Results from the healthy group are presented directly (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports fMRI experiments using social tasks (Prisoner’s Dilemma, Ultimatum/Welfare games) that explicitly manipulate sociality (acquaintance vs. random individual; human vs. computer). Participants are healthy adults (college and community samples; Pilot N=10, Main N=15; ages ≥18). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (FSL and SPM analyses; cluster thresholds and coordinates reported; Table 4 and other tables/figures give MNI coordinates and statistics), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables and described in text/figures. Connectivity (PPI) is reported but not the sole analysis. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study tested facial color processing (a form of social communication/perception of others) using task-evoked BOLD responses to natural vs. bluish faces in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 25.2). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) and presents group-level activations (figures and table) used to define ROIs. Thus it meets: I3 (social-related task: facial color/social perception), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task contrast reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an event-related fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (humor styles differing by target: self vs others, and motivation: benign vs detrimental), which maps onto social constructs such as perception/understanding of self and others and affiliation. Sample: 42 healthy adult participants aged 20–30, meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level task-evoked contrasts and voxelwise activation results with coordinates and statistical thresholds (FWE-corrected peaks, cluster reports, and tables of activations), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; whole-brain contrasts and tables of coordinates are clearly described. Although ROI and PPI analyses are also reported, whole-brain, group-level task effects for the healthy sample are present. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study that includes a social-related task (gaze stimuli) and reports group-level whole-brain task activation in a healthy adult (neurotypical) control group. The neurotypical group (N=15; mean age 24.6±6.5) is within the 18–65 range and their within-group random-effects contrasts (incongruent>congruent for gaze and arrow conditions) are reported and presented as whole-brain maps and in a coordinates table (Table 2 and figures). Thus the paper provides task-evoked, group-level, whole-brain activation results for healthy adults during social processing (gaze), satisfying I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contains within-group healthy maps; participants are adults; empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (mutual direct vs averted gaze in dynamic virtual characters) addressing social cognition/understanding of others, and includes a separate healthy adult control group. The manuscript provides whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group (within-group and whole-brain contrasts reported in text, tables, and figures), not only ROI analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging, analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain and ROI imaging results for controls), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports fMRI of social cognition using a validated, naturalistic Theory of Mind task (MASC), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=18, age range 20–45), meeting the sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results (GLM contrasts ToM vs PI) with thresholding, cluster correction, and tabulated coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy/control sample are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and not a non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This empirical fMRI study investigates self- and mother-referential processing and an abstract social attribution task (SAT), which are social-related constructs (affiliation/attachment; perception/understanding of self and others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=17 analyzed, mean age 21.5) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and statistics (composite t-maps, conjunctions, tables of peak coordinates, FDR-corrected maps and uncorrected contrasts) clearly from the healthy/control group. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, figures/tables/coordinates).

This is an fMRI study of social processing: eye contact modulation of spontaneous mimicry (social perception/communication). Participants: 20 healthy adults (mean age 23), so sample meets the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, Incongruent > Congruent, Direct > Averted, interaction), thresholded and cluster-level FWE-corrected, with results presented in Table 1 and Figures (coordinates reported). This is not an ROI-only or connectivity-only paper (although DCM is included, whole-brain task activations are reported). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–40) using a social cognition task (Implicit Association Test with politicians’ faces and names) probing social-related processing (attitudes toward others). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR correction and voxelwise tables/figures), clearly from the healthy/control group, with reported contrasts and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Study used task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (modified Cyberball) in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.1). The paper reports both ROI-based MVPA and an exploratory whole-brain searchlight analysis with group-level, whole-brain corrected results (significant STS coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked group-level maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5; I6 is also satisfied because whole-brain results are reported as MNI coordinates and described in text.

The study uses task-based fMRI to examine perception of biological motion (point-light walkers), which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 28.2), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs. scrambled biological motion) with corrected voxelwise results and provides MNI coordinates and cluster tables/figures. Thus it satisfies the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of empathic decision-making (social processing: empathy/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (GLM whole-brain results reported at cluster-corrected P<0.05 with tables of activations and conjunctions) and describes whole-brain PPI analyses; whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study used event-related fMRI while healthy adult participants (n=16 scanned, 14 included in analysis; ages 18–30) performed a social-evaluative task (trustworthiness judgments vs age judgments). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPMs), with coordinates and tables of activations (including small-volume corrected results and whole-brain contrasts), and describes task-evoked effects for the healthy control group. Thus it provides whole-brain task activation maps from healthy adults during a social-related task and meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.4) that investigates processing of angry prosody—a social-communication/emotion perception task—using a dichotic listening paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, whole-brain contrasts) with coordinates and cluster results for healthy participants. Results for the healthy sample are presented directly (not only subgroup or connectivity analyses). Thus it meets the meta-analysis focus on fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (imagined triadic interactions vs self/other/control), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., triad > iron; triad > (self & other)) with whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates/tables and figures. Results for the healthy control group are clearly reported and not limited to ROI- or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task relevance, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

The study uses fMRI in a social-related task (biological motion perception) and includes a healthy adult sample, but it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group within this paper. fMRI results and whole-brain activation maps are presented for the single patient (SL) only; comparisons to ‘healthy participants’ are made by reference to prior work rather than by reporting an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group map in the present article. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed approaching characters making happy or angry expressions (social-related task assessing affiliation/dominance). Sample includes ten healthy young adult participants (healthy adults). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with statistical thresholding, cluster coordinates, voxel counts, and figures—satisfying whole-brain task-evoked map reporting. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within adult range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social decision-making (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 23–38). It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (conjunction and task contrasts such as COMP>COOP), cluster-level multiple-comparison correction, and reports results in figures/tables (coordinates and SPMs). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment explicitly manipulating social processing (live social interaction vs. non-social avatar) and analyzes healthy adult participants (ages 20–26). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., social vs. non-social; autobiographical vs. non-autobiographical) with statistical thresholding and FDR correction, and results are presented in figures/tables. This is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social communication processing in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22). The task examines processing of communicative vs noncommunicative vocal sounds (social communication). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (vocal > nonvocal and communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded with FDR q<.05 and provides peak coordinates and whole-brain activation maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used task-based fMRI of naturalistic social (theory-of-mind) processing, includes a healthy adult control group (n=22, ages 19–46) with results reported separately, and reports whole-brain, group-level within-group task contrasts (ToM > physical inference) for the control group with cluster-corrected activations and coordinate tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (action understanding) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32). The task is social-related (why/how/what observation goals) and uses task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses. Although main analyses were restricted to an a priori mask of mirror neuron and mentalizing systems, the manuscript explicitly notes that details about the mask and whole-brain results are provided in the Supplemental Methods, and group-level random-effects analyses were conducted and reported (cluster coordinates/tables and figures). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I5), and acceptability of coordinate/figure reporting (I6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (10 right-handed males) who viewed funny vs. non-funny cartoons (a social-communication/humor task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with coordinates and statistical values (Talairach X,Y,Z and Z-values, p<0.001 uncorrected) linking BOLD responses to trait cheerfulness; these are clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perception and understanding of self/others (social-related task), meeting the review scope. Sample: 30 healthy adult participants (15M/15F), ages ~26, within 18–65, with results reported separately for healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (thresholds, cluster correction, coordinates, and tables/figures), not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related mentalizing task) and I4 (reports a healthy adult control group, n=33, ages 18–42). However, it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain analysis described is a between-group contrast (Controls > ASC). Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (perception of others' eye gaze and social attention) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts to identify face-responsive regions (clusters selected with z>4 and cluster-size thresholds), and provides atlas coordinates and tables/figures of activations using SPM. Thus it meets criteria for using fMRI during a social task (I3), includes healthy adults in the 18–65 range (I4), reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I5), and provides coordinates/figures as acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used task-based fMRI during an autobiographical emotion recall paradigm (self-referential emotional processing — a social-related construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults aged 21–50 (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses at the group level (two-way ANOVA interactions and within-group contrasts, permutation-based voxel and cluster thresholds) and describes significant clusters and contrasts in the text, satisfying I5 and I6. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state only, and includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=27, ages within 18–65) that used task-based fMRI to examine social interaction processing (cooperative vs. affective interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinate tables and figures (FWE-corrected and uncorrected results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task fMRI of social perception and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper’s whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported only as between-group contrasts (patient vs control). The authors do not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (i.e., no whole-brain HC social>nonsocial map is presented; within-group HC effects are reported only via post-hoc ROI analyses based on between-group clusters). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using Heider-&-Simmel-style animations to probe agency attribution and mentalizing, which is a social-related task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (12 in fMRI; mean age 25.2), meeting the age/sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (high>low and low>high), analyzed with SPM2 and reported activations across many brain regions at a voxelwise threshold (p<0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

Although this fMRI study used a social task (Cyberball) and reports group-level whole-brain maps and coordinate tables/figures, it included both healthy adults (n=37) and a clinical subgroup with SAD (n=9) but did not report group-level whole-brain results separately for the healthy-only group. The meta-analysis requires that when clinical groups are included, results for the healthy group be reported separately. Here the primary one-sample t-tests and regression analyses are reported for the entire sample (combined healthy and SAD) rather than a clearly identified healthy/control group. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by the paper’s reporting format.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social reward (meets I3) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (meets I6). Participants are aged 18–21 (within adult range), but the sample is a mixed clinical/healthy sample and all reported whole-brain results and regressions are from the combined sample rather than from a clearly identified healthy/control group. The paper does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map explicitly identified as coming from a healthy adult control group. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of charitable donation decisions (social/moral decision-making), involving healthy adult participants (n=19; mean age 28.2) and a task that probes social-related constructs (altruism, attachment/aversion to societal causes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mesolimbic, orbitofrontal, anterior PFC activations) with reported thresholds and cluster criteria; coordinates and tables are referenced in the text/supporting information. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, subjects, image acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (implicit interpersonal space/affiliation) in healthy adults, reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (main effects and treatment×stimulus interaction) from the healthy sample. The sample comprises healthy adult males (ages 19–30). Whole-brain random-effects GLM results are described (significant clusters in dorsal striatum, ACC, medial frontal gyrus) and PPI connectivity is additionally reported; whole-brain task activation maps/cluster results are presented in the text/figures. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (explicit labeling of others’ brief emotional facial expressions), scanned healthy adult participants (N=50, ages 18–29), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group-level contrasts and regression results (with cluster-level FWE correction) clearly identified for the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of person-related (social) memory and knowledge retrieval (status, personality traits, identity), using task fMRI in healthy adult participants (Study 1: n=24, Mage≈23; Study 2: n=26, Mage≈20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate GLM contrasts (e.g., all memory > baseline; status > baseline; trait > baseline; face > name; name > face) thresholded at voxel-level FWE P<0.05 and provides coordinates/tables and figures for these maps. Thus it satisfies social task fMRI (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I5), with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only connectivity, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study investigating learning about others’ preference similarity—a social cognitive task (affiliation/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.1) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (conjunction analyses, cluster-corrected activations, MNI coordinates) for the healthy participant group (e.g., dmPFC, caudate, precuneus, AG, STS), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, model-based fMRI analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognitive task (judging political statements) that probes perception/understanding of self and others and broader social cognition. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 22–45) and the study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (SPM random-effects second-level analyses, whole-brain thresholds reported, ROI corrections noted) with result tables and figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so article is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (memory for faces with emotional expressions—perception/understanding of others) in healthy adult participants (n=35, mean age 29). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) and provides Talairach coordinates and cluster tables/figures for emotion and load contrasts, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception with emotional and neutral faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 30 years) reported separately from the clinical Social Phobia group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task vs. rest contrasts and within-group deactivation maps for both groups, using whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and reporting clusters in DMN regions for the healthy group; these constitute qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Exclusion reason: E5 applies — the study includes only children (mean ages ~12–13) and does not include a healthy adult (18–65) group or subgroup. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social-related processing — self/other face recognition), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the control/typically-developing group), and I6 (whole-brain results are described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult participants aged 18–65 reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E2 met: the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) fMRI analyses with no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses task-based fMRI of social processing — social closeness judgments with friends vs unfamiliar faces) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps are reported; fMRI results are presented via ROI extractions rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts). Although the full text is complete and the study reports task fMRI in healthy adults, failure to provide whole-brain, group-level task activation maps means it cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during socially relevant tasks (round-robin face-viewing and person-judgment tasks) that probe perception/understanding of others (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=26, mean age 28.7) meeting the 18–65 criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects parametric whole-brain regression; Fig. S1 and Table S4) clearly from the healthy sample, satisfying I5 and I6. The manuscript therefore meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (modified Cyberball) examining social exclusion, empathy, and cooperative/competitive behavior—directly addressing social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (Chinese males, ages 18–27), satisfying the sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., exclusion>inclusion during OBSERVE; treatment effects and an mOFC cluster during PLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and voxelwise thresholding, and these group-level healthy-participant results are clearly described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effects, age range appropriate, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This study reports an fMRI task probing emotion perception (perception/understanding of others; social communication) using dynamic facial and vocal stimuli — clearly a social-related task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 19–24 and mean 19.67), reported separately. The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked group analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, PFWE<0.05) with tables/figures of activations rather than ROI-only results. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (joint attention) in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI probing social communication/joint attention; (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (n=32, ages ~24.5, 18–65 range); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., IJA vs SA, RJA vs SA, conjunctions) with cluster correction; (I6) whole-brain results and coordinates are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-group healthy task activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of others’ emotional facial expressions, including affiliation-relevant emotions like happiness and disgust), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=40, mean age 29.5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (family-wise error-corrected cluster threshold, voxelwise P<0.001) with coordinates and ROI results clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/thresholds). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using an interaction categorization task comparing human–human and human–robot interactions. Sample: 26 healthy adult participants aged 18–35. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (univariate whole-brain contrasts HHI > HRI and HRI > HHI with voxelwise and cluster thresholds) and provides peak coordinates and cluster results; parametric and ROI analyses are also reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reports whole-brain group results (I5) with coordinates/details (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study that implemented a social-related task (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment; Theory of Mind/social cognition), recruited a healthy adult sample (N=19, ages within 18–65), and reported group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects contrasts G−N, E−N, G−E, E−G) with coordinate tables and figures. Whole-brain statistical thresholds and extent criteria are described, and regression analyses with group-level maps are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study directly examines processing of CT-targeted affective touch—a social-affiliation/affective touch paradigm—using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 19–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, arm>palm) with correction procedures and cluster thresholds and presents tables/figures of these results. A PPI connectivity analysis is also reported but does not replace the whole-brain task maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of vocal versus non-vocal sound processing, which the authors frame as socially relevant (voice processing/social communication). Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (vocal > non-vocal contrasts) with statistical thresholds described and displayed in figures. Thus it satisfies the social-related fMRI task requirement, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task results. Resting-state analyses are supplementary and do not prevent inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an empathy task (social cognition) with both schizophrenia patients and a matched healthy control group (N=14). The paper reports within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) one-sample t-test results for the healthy/control group, including cluster tables and figures, with SPM8 and corrected thresholds (AlphaSim/SVC). Healthy participants are adults within the 18–65 range. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI task examining social sharing/affiliation (participants view emotional pictures either together with a friend or alone), meets the social-related construct (affiliation), and tests healthy adult participants (ages 20–33). The paper presents group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) with appropriate correction as well as ROI results; these healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion IDs met: E2, E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. 

Rationale: The study used task fMRI with a social-affective (empathic fear) cinematic stimulus and reports results for a healthy adult control group (satisfying I3 and I4). However, the manuscript does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Analyses focus on network-cohesion indices derived from meta-analytic ROIs and connectivity/time-series comparisons (NCI) rather than unmasked whole-brain activation maps. Thus it meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI/connectivity-focused without whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=8; ages 23–28) using task-evoked manipulation of social/affiliative emotion (tenderness) and negative emotion (anguish), i.e., social-related processing (affiliation/attachment). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (fixed-effects) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables of local maxima for Tenderness vs Anguish and Anguish vs Tenderness, and also small-volume corrected ROI results; these whole-brain maps are clearly identified as coming from the healthy participants. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group-only; participants are within 18–65; empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related 3T fMRI study of implicit mentalizing using a game-theoretic “Chicken” task (social interaction) in healthy adults. The sample comprised 16 healthy male adults (mean age 21.9), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (one-sample t-tests; FDR-corrected whole-brain results) and provides coordinates in Table 1 and activation figures, fulfilling the whole-brain reporting requirement. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; not between-group-only; participants are in the 18–65 range; empirical fMRI data reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing using the DISC social-attribution task in a sample of healthy adults (N=22, ages 18–25). The study reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., FRIENDS > WATCH and FRIENDS > SIZE) with appropriate voxelwise/statistical thresholding and correction (cluster thresholding and permutation testing with TFCE/FWE), clearly describing results from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (viewing realistic first-person social interaction videos) in a healthy adult sample (n=20 males, mean age 24.6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected thresholds) with peak coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Behavioral and imaging results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (mental state attribution/intentional stance) in healthy adults. The analyzed sample (N=12; ages 21–31) is within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Composer > Computer) entered into a second-level random-effects analysis, with coordinates and cluster thresholds provided (tables and figures). Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging results directly target perception/understanding of others, meeting the meta-analysis objectives.

This fMRI study directly investigates perception of social cooperation (a social-related task) using task-based fMRI (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=19) reported separately from the patient group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts for the healthy control group (e.g., C+ > C–, FDR-corrected, reported coordinates and figures) meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper issues). Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of impression formation (perception/understanding of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (18–30 years, n=18 included). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (incongruent vs. congruent contrasts), with cluster-level results surviving FDR correction and coordinates presented in tables/figures. Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps relevant to social processing.

Only abstract and metadata provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract, the study uses task fMRI in a social decision context, so I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) appears satisfied. However, the provided content does not report participant ages (cannot confirm 18–65), nor does it provide methods/results to verify a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5) or that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I6). Therefore I4, I5, and I6 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be reliably applied based on the incomplete text. Recommend obtaining the full text to verify age range and whether whole-brain task activation maps are reported before inclusion.

This fMRI study measures neural responses while healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) listened to literary story excerpts and explicitly models mentalizing and action content. The task targets social cognition (mentalizing/theory-of-mind) which maps to the review’s social-related processing constructs. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (Mentalizing vs Action and vice versa) with appropriate multiple-comparisons correction and displays whole-brain results in the Results/figures. The sample is healthy adults and results are reported for that group. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion regulation using angry faces (a social stimulus) with healthy adult participants (N=60, age range 18–57). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry) with coordinates, tables, and figures describing healthy-group effects. Resting-state analyses are additional but the study includes task-evoked whole-brain results for the healthy sample. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, sample within 18–65, and empirical). Hence it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9) that explicitly manipulates a social interaction (human–human vs human–machine competition) to engage Theory of Mind/social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrasts such as [H(I+C)>M(I+C)], [I(H+M)>C(H+M)], interaction [H(I>C)]>[M(I>C)]) with voxelwise thresholding (P<0.001 uncorrected) and tables/figures listing activated clusters and Talairach/MNI coordinates. Results for the healthy sample are presented clearly. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps reported (tables and figures).

This full-text reports an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 33.5) using social tasks (imitation, expressive suppression, and gender decision) in response to dynamic facial expressions — meeting the review’s social-processing task requirement. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., IMT>eSUP, IMT>GND) with statistical thresholds and activation coordinates reported in tables/figures, clearly identified as healthy-group results. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no evidence of truncated content. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (self-other touch) in adults, reporting separate neurotypical control group data. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts for neurotypical controls (figures and text) with FWE correction. Sample ages (controls mean 23.7±3.6; ADHD and NC are adults) fall within 18–65. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for healthy group), and I6 (maps reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during an emotional face discrimination task (social processing of others’ expressions), in a sample of 38 healthy adults (mean age 27.5), satisfying the sample criterion. It provides a second-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise group contrast (FACES>OBJECTS) with SPM results, cluster statistics, figures (SPM t-maps), and VOI analyses described in the text and supplementary material. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), and I6 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Inclusion criteria applied: I3,I4,I5,I6. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This study used task fMRI of a social cognition paradigm (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) so I3 is satisfied, and it includes a healthy control group of young adults assessed with SCID/CIDI so I4 is satisfied. However, the paper reports mainly between-group (high-risk vs low-risk) voxelwise comparisons and does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map (or main effect) for the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and must be excluded per E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This fMRI study investigates social communication (speech act comprehension: Naming vs. Requesting) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–41). It reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., “Request > Naming”) with FDR-corrected results and provides coordinates/tables and figures, clearly identifying effects from the healthy/control sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study using a validated social ‘Theory of Mind’ visual task (moving triangles) meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults aged 24–64 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R; ToM > Baseline) with statistical thresholds, peak coordinates, and tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). The full text content appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a social-context (cooperation vs competition vs individual) task and viewed empathy-evoking stimuli while undergoing fMRI. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=16, mean age 23.2) are within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts and conjunction analyses) with coordinate tables and thresholding details. Reporting includes whole-brain results and ROI/SVC procedures; results for the healthy sample are presented directly. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/inferring others’ preferences) using task-based functional MRI. Participants were healthy adults (n=64; ages 18–26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (parametric modulation by self–other discrepancy), with voxelwise thresholds, cluster sizes, and MNI coordinates (Table 1, figures, and Methods). Results are reported for the healthy participant group and not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study directly tests social-communicative actions (e.g., waving, greeting) using task-based fMRI and contrasts social-communicative versus manipulation actions. It reports data from healthy adult participants (N=36 included in analyses; ages 18–28). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (social vs. manipulation, and each vs. baseline) with thresholds and tables/figures described in the text and Supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, are not solely connectivity/resting-state, and include healthy adult whole-brain task activations. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social attribution (self-responsibility and self-serving bias) using task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants (12 neurologically healthy males, ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; fixed-effects and follow-up random-effects ROI testing) with results presented as voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables. The task is clearly social-related (attribution of positive/negative social events). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of empathy for others' pain (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=13, mean age 33) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and provides figures and tables of voxelwise activations and coordinates for the control group (within-group contrasts and main effects), not limited to ROIs. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages ~25) investigating social reward (smiling avatar) during real-time fMRI neurofeedback of the ACC. The task involves social-related processing (social reward/positive facial expression) used as feedback, meeting the review’s social-processing construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and FWE-corrected group analyses (NF, transfer, generalization) clearly attributable to the healthy participant groups. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an explicit social judgment (approachability) task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports their data separately alongside clinical groups (meets I4). The methods describe second-level within-group contrasts (social vs baseline/gender) for each group, and the manuscript and supplementary material report within-group whole-brain task activation results (meets I5 and I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates event simulation including social situations (41% of stimuli depicted social interactions) and explicitly discusses social-cognitive processes (e.g., theory of mind). Participants are healthy adults (N=20, mean age 20.65), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Imp–Con, Exp–Imp, Ftr–Exp) analyzed with SPM8 using random-effects second-level one-sample t-tests and reports cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates; tables/figures of activation are described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately. However, the imaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses (STSp and MT) localized within individuals; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. A whole-brain search is described but focused on schizophrenia patients, and no unmasked healthy-group whole-brain statistical map or coordinate table of a healthy-group whole-brain contrast is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence for the healthy group) is not met. Exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (team membership, perception of others) in healthy adult participants using task-based fMRI. The methods and results report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., single-video vs baseline; own-team vs other-team; paired judgments vs press task) with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates. Sample comprises healthy, right-handed adult volunteers (age range reported 17–43; majority are adults and analyses are reported at the healthy-group level). Reporting includes whole-brain statistical maps/tables and coordinates. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and provides clearly described within-group task activation results appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of social interaction and reactive aggression using an interactive Taylor paradigm (social perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adult males (N=16, mean age 28.6), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. Analyses used SPM2 with random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise statistics reported (thresholds, conjunctions, coordinates, activation maps and tables) for group-level task effects (retaliation, watching opponent, anticipation), and ROI splits by psychopathy are secondary; whole-brain healthy-group results are clearly presented. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria for task-based social fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting (coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study examines haptic and visual identification of basic facial expressions, which is social processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (sighted and early blind), ages within 18–65, with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM random-effects group analyses), thresholding, coordinates, tables, and conjunction analyses for sighted and early blind groups; these are clear healthy-group task activation maps. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (judgments about self, friends, and strangers; constructs: perception/understanding of self and others, affiliation/attachment). Participants are healthy adults (n=98, mean age 20.7) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and maps (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) presented in figures and described in the text (thresholded at p < 0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (joint attention) and reports results for a healthy control group, fulfilling I3 and I4. However, the reported fMRI results are analyzed primarily using small-volume (ROI) corrections focused on five a priori ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (only ROI/SVC results and ROI peaks are reported). Therefore it fails to meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of laughter perception (social communication) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26). Tasks explicitly probe social/emotional processing (explicit emotional classification; implicit bout counting) and thus address social-related constructs (social communication; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts and conjunctions reported, tables of activations, ROI and whole-brain results), clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-referential relationship episodes) in healthy adults (final sample n=35). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with cluster inference (FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of significant clusters. Results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Reporting includes voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain task fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social reward processing (social incentive delay task) in healthy adult participants (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). The paper reports within-group task-evoked neural activations including whole-brain results and small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results; whole-brain activations and coordinate tables are described (e.g., Tables 2–4, whole-brain FWE-corrected results). Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly and separately. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial expression/identity processing (social perception of others) in healthy adults (mean age 25.6; N=11 analyzed). The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain correction for non-ROI areas and presents statistical parametric maps and coordinate-based results for task contrasts (e.g., interaction and main-effect contrasts), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked results. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the sample consists of adolescents (mean age 15.45, range 13.22–17.18), so no healthy adult group aged 18–65 is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social/mentalizing processes: SelfOther and Stories tasks), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps are reported), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in the main text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult participants aged 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults due to participant age.

This fMRI study tested emotion modulation of trained visuomotor (mirror) responses in a sample of healthy adults (n=19, mean age 27.7) using a task involving action/shape observation preceded by emotional IAPS images. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (untrained>trained; whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected results in SMA and IFG) and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—the MNS/emotion/social cognition domain), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to ROI-only analyses, not connectivity/resting-only, not restricted to out-of-range ages, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based BOLD imaging in healthy adult participants (15 right-handed males aged 18–40). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds, peak coordinates, conjunctions, and figures/tables describing healthy-group task effects (sad vs neutral; condition contrasts). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult samples, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using audiovisual biographies of suffering others and donation decisions—clearly probing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others; affiliation/compassion). The sample comprises N=57 healthy adults (mean age ~29), within the 18–65 range. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (pre-to-post-intervention contrasts), whole-brain gray-matter regressions with coordinates, exploratory whole-brain results, and shares maps via NeuroVault and GitHub. Results pertain to the healthy participant groups (not limited to a subgroup). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social gaze (face/gaze-shift) stimulus during a task that probes social-related processing and action control. Sample: 23 healthy adults aged 21–37 (within 18–65). Analysis: voxelwise, whole-brain second-level random-effects SPM analyses are reported (main effects, interactions, cluster-level corrected maps and coordinates reported in text/tables/figures). The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked activations in healthy adults during a social task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Participants are adolescents (ages 12–18) rather than healthy adults aged 18–65, so the study does not meet the sample age inclusion criterion (I4). The paper does report an fMRI social task (implicit facial emotion processing) (I3), and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the control group (I5) with results described in the text/figures (I6). However because all participants are outside the specified adult age range and no separate healthy adult subgroup (18–65) is reported, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (college students) performing a social-related task (observation of others' goal-directed hand actions; relates to Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample activation maps for the non-alexithymic (healthy control) group and the alexithymic group, with statistical thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample consists of healthy adults (ages consistent with college sample) and results for the healthy subgroup (non-ALEX) are reported separately. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using an implicit social recognition (face-matching) task in healthy adult participants (20 males, age 18–43). It presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level paired t-tests) with cluster-based whole-brain family-wise error correction and reports peak coordinates, t-values, and cluster extents for effects in the left TPJ. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy adult whole-brain task effects, ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of co-speech gesture processing during naturalistic narrative comprehension, which falls under social communication/social-related processing. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (ages 22–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID; speech > gestures+speech; gestures+speech > speech; interaction effects) with coordinates, cluster extents, tables and figures, and multiple whole-brain statistical thresholds. It is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group task effects. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-attribution (Theory of Mind) task (People vs Bumper) and reports results for a healthy adult control group. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (People - Bumper) and presents group maps and ROI tables for the control (CON) group separately from the recovered-anorexia (RAN) group, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, healthy adults within 18–65, and original empirical data). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 24.4) that investigates social-context modulation of empathy for others' pain. The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others' pain/intentionality). The paper reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (main effects and interactions) with coordinates and FDR-corrected results across the healthy sample. Results are presented in tables and figures and report group-level activation maps and PPI connectivity, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation vs deception) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 22–38). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain ToM vs non-ToM with reported peaks, figures, and coordinate tables) and subsequent ROI comparisons based on those whole-brain results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures).
