No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. The task probes social cognition (legal responsibility and punishment judgments — perception and understanding of others), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed; age range 18–45), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (whole-brain main effects and whole-brain contrasts with Talairach coordinates and t-values; tables/regions described), satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (ROI and whole-brain analyses), and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI assessing self-related olfactory evaluation (a social-related construct: Perception/Understanding of Self). Participants were healthy adult women (ages 18–35), and group-level fMRI contrasts (e.g., ‘self’-peptide minus solvent; ‘self’-peptide minus ‘non-self’-peptide) were computed using SPM and reported with MNI coordinates and thresholds. The paper states that whole-brain analysis was performed and provides voxelwise activation coordinates and statistical values for group contrasts in the healthy sample. Results are reported in the main text and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social/self task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (coordinates/figures provided). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment on observation and motor imagery of face and limb movements, explicitly addressing social communication and gesture processing (social-related task). Participants were healthy adults (n=14, mean age 25.2). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects ANOVA, SPM2) with FWE-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Results for the healthy control sample are reported directly (no exclusive subgroup-only or patient contrasts). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy age group only, non-empirical) are met. Thus the paper satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Although this study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social processing: Social emotion/Belief tasks) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=17), the full text only reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (typically developing > ASD) and region coordinates for group differences. The manuscript does not present or clearly identify an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no control-group one-sample whole-brain results or coordinate table/figure explicitly labeled as the healthy group main effect are provided). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map reported) is not met. Full text appears complete. Hence the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based EEG-fMRI study of minimal-group social processing (group categorization) in healthy adults (N=20 analyzed; mean age 23.4). The experiment uses functional MRI concurrent with EEG during a social task addressing affiliation and perception of others. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses (thresholding described; cluster-level FWE correction; activations and MNI coordinates presented in Table 1 and figures) linking BOLD activity (mPFC, STS/TPJ) to EEG components. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study investigated social feedback processing (self/other trait feedback) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult German and Chinese participants (ages within 18–65). The experiment involved social interaction and an in-scanner feedback task probing social cognition constructs (self/other understanding, social conformity, positivity bias). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation results (main effects and contrasts) with tables of coordinates and FWE-corrected clusters (e.g., MPFC/ACC, TPJ, ventral striatum), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (dynamic and static facial-expression perception), includes a healthy adult control group (N=13, ages within 18–65) whose results are reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group (simple main effect of dynamic vs. static faces with whole-brain correction). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. The full text provided contains background, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete.

The study uses fMRI in healthy adult controls (n=10) and reports whole-brain group activation maps, but the task is a monetary-reward continuous performance task (attention/reward), not a social-related task. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for controls), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (task is not social-related; constructs like social communication, affiliation, or perception of others are not the task focus). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

E4 met: The paper reports only between-group contrasts (ALS patients vs healthy controls) and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map (main effect or within-group contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task fMRI of social-related processing: facial emotion perception) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages within 18–65, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study interrogates social-related processing of dynamic facial expressions (meets I3) and includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (TD; ages within 18–65) analyzed separately (meets I4). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., a within-group or main-effect map for TD participants). The whole-brain analyses described in the Methods and Results appear to have been used to test between-group effects (two-sample t-tests) and found no significant group-difference clusters; voxelwise results specific to the healthy group (TD) are not reported. The paper primarily reports ROI-based results and DCM (effective connectivity) analyses. Because the manuscript reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, it violates exclusion criterion E4 and therefore is excluded.

This fMRI study uses a social-interactive task (pseudo-interactive joke task) and includes a healthy control group (TD adults) analyzed separately, but it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps for the healthy/control group. The authors explicitly state they focused on an a priori ROI (arMPFC) and could not perform whole-brain or connectivity analyses due to signal loss. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) but fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported) and thus meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a resting-state fMRI study (ICA/FNC) comparing ASD and TD groups; it does not use a task-based social processing paradigm and does not report any healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. The sample spans children and adolescents (ABIDE II age range includes 5–64 years) and no separate healthy adult (18–65) group results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI/social task), I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately), and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy group). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses without a healthy-group task map), E4 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect; only between-group/resting contrasts), and E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no separate adult-only healthy subgroup). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social touch (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants. Sample: 40 healthy heterosexual males (mean age 25.8), meeting the adult age range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activations with MNI coordinates, statistical values, and PFWE-corrected clusters (text, figures, and supplementary tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of real-time social interaction (group vs. individual problem solving), meeting the review objective. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–45) drawn from non-clinical populations. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., collective > individual silent periods) with FDR correction and describes the maps and cluster coordinates; whole-brain results are presented and compared to control task. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study used task-based fMRI to examine neural responses to emotional speech prosody (a social-communication/social-perception task) in healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results (emotional > neutral prosody) with cluster-corrected statistics and figures/tables describing these effects. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gaze and social voice cues vs arrows/tones) addressing social communication/perception (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (N=22, mean age ~23) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM12 random-effects, whole-brain thresholds and small-volume corrections) and reports results in text/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, includes participants in the 18–65 range, and is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related interpersonal distance (affiliation) task; (I4) the sample includes healthy adult participants (19 males, ages 18–30) with results reported for the healthy group; (I5) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, FDR q<0.05) with reported main effects and treatment×protagonist interaction and listed brain regions; (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text (with follow-up ROI analyses reported separately). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study used task-based fMRI of a social/caregiving stimulus (baby schema), so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, the sample consists exclusively of recently detoxified opioid-dependent patients with no healthy adult/control group reported separately, so I4 (healthy adult group present) is not met. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, but only for the clinical patient group and does not provide an unmasked whole-brain task effect for a healthy/control group, so I5 is not met. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (no healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (self-related judgments) in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during self-judgment (a social-related construct: Perception/Understanding of Self), includes a healthy adult sample (n=24; ages within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables (and figures) of task-evoked activations. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during clearly social-related tasks (Social Attribution; Social Identity; Physical Identity) satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (CN; n=18; ages 18–42) satisfying I4. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise activation maps and cluster tables for the healthy/control group (e.g., clusters in CN during People–Bumper and Identity contrasts; explicit whole-brain voxel-wide comparisons described), fulfilling I5 and I6. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results (group maps and cluster tables), and Discussion, and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of joint social interaction (leading/following/mutual) with haptic contact, directly addressing social-processing constructs (social communication, perception of others, mentalizing, social reward). Sample comprises healthy adult dancers (mean age 40.4, within 18–65) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, FDR-corrected maps, and tables of Talairach coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (figures/tables and text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24) that uses action observation/execution paradigms probing mirror-system responses—relevant to social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (explicit whole-brain thresholding at p<0.001 uncorrected and ROI analyses with FWE correction) and provides peak coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (learning about others’ generosity) with a computationally matched non-social control (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 19–37; N=30 recruited, N=26 analyzed) meeting the 18–65 requirement and results are reported for the healthy group (I4). The article reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, one-sample t-tests, cluster-correction) with coordinates and tables/figures (I5, I6). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references) is present in the provided text and is sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore include.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception), includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, mean age ~25) reported separately, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation results for the healthy/control group (see Table 2; P<0.001 uncorrected). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study).

The study uses task-based fMRI to probe evaluative judgments/self-referential processing (social cognition/theory of mind), includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 26.4 within 18–65) analyzed separately, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinates for the control group (figures and tables). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–24) investigating communicative speech production, a social communication task involving perception and understanding of others. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (communication vs description, task vs control) with statistical thresholds and tables/figures of activated cortical areas and peak coordinates. Results are reported for the healthy/control group and include whole-brain analyses rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only approaches. Thus it meets the review objective and satisfies the required reporting and sample criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face processing (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (CA group; mean age 31 years) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and displays group activation maps (e.g., Figure 3: mean z-score images for CA controls, P<0.05 corrected) and describes voxelwise ANOVA and correction procedures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=18 after exclusion, mean age 21.5) that uses a social interaction task (rock-paper-scissors played against perceived human, humanoid robot with AI, and random computer) addressing perception/understanding of others and mentalizing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Int–Rnd, Art–Rnd, Int–Art) thresholded and presented in figures/tables and ROI follow-ups; coordinates and thresholding are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a clearly social task (VISTTA inducing verbal social rejection), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–30 (female), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and detailed reported clusters/coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=29; ages 20–35) performing explicit and implicit facial emotion/age discrimination tasks, which are social-cognitive (perception/understanding of others). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and SPM random-effects results are reported (FWE-corrected maps and contrasts), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and supplemented by ROI analyses. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using a social interactive task (virtual handshake) probing social rejection — a social-related construct (mentalizing/perception of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (refusal vs acceptance) are reported (regions, thresholds, cluster correction described). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study examines social communication (dynamic facial expressions) in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4), the reported analyses and results are restricted to ROI/small-volume-corrected statistics. The paper documents ROI-based SPM analyses (small volume correction using WFU PickAtlas) and reports FWE-corrected peaks within those ROIs; conjunction and interaction tests were conducted within specified ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain thresholded maps or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported independent of ROI/SVC). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and is excluded under E2 (ROI-only results).

This is an original fMRI study of social communication (vitality forms) in healthy adults (N=18, ages ~25), using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (vitality vs. control), conjunctions, coordinates (MNI), and PFWE-corrected results (Table 1, figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (adequate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines voice-identity processing (speaker recognition and vocal vs. non-vocal listening), which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports data from healthy adult control groups (n=32; age ranges ~29–34; individually reported and matched to cases) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM second-level contrasts for controls; within-group activation maps and tables of coordinates are reported for contrasts such as vocal>non-vocal and speaker>speech). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables, with significance thresholds described, and figures/tables showing control-group activations. Although the paper also includes single-case vs. control comparisons and PPI connectivity analyses, it clearly provides unmasked healthy-group task activation effects. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes task (social perception/understanding of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American adults aged 18–27). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (mass-univariate GLM in SPM5) and multiple group contrasts and tables/figures of activations (e.g., RME − GD, same- vs other-culture contrasts), clearly identified as coming from the healthy groups. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, participant ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendix).

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI with dynamic happy and fearful facial expressions (a social/emotion recognition task); (I4) includes healthy adult participants (control group and non-psychotic familial-risk participants in early twenties, within 18–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the groups (figures and text describe within-group activation/deactivation maps thresholded Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, whole-brain maps for healthy groups are provided, task-based activations (not only connectivity) are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study directly investigating interpersonal (social) emotion regulation, which is a social cognitive process (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM8 flexible factorial design) with results presented as whole-brain contrasts and tables of coordinates (reported at p<0.001 uncorrected), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain contrasts with coordinate tables), Discussion, and Limitations, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study (20 participants) that investigates integration of faces and voices — a social perceptual/communication task relevant to social processing. The abstract reports group-level voxelwise activation results using multiple statistical criteria (identifying regions such as hippocampus, occipital and temporal cortices) and PPI connectivity analyses. Thus the paper reports whole-brain task-evoked effects for a healthy participant group. No evidence that results are ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical. Based on the provided full-text information, all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI task activation mapping appear satisfied.

This study uses fMRI during social-cognitive tasks (action observation/understanding) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (control) task activation map or main-effect/within-group HC contrast. Reported whole-brain results are primarily between-group contrasts (ALS > HC and HC > ALS) and subgroup analyses; there is no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect (HC main effect) presented in the full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

The study reports an fMRI experiment probing social-related processing: participants judged meaning (social/semantic) versus physical properties of LEGO models, and contrasts probe self/other and collective/individual effects (social cognition constructs). Sample consists of healthy adults (n=25, mean age 24). Analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results using SPM8 with random-effects second-level tests; results are presented with peak coordinates, tables and figures and corrected thresholds. Thus the paper provides healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked activations relevant to social processing and satisfies the inclusion criteria below.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants interacted with a virtual agent and the task probes social communication/affiliation and perception of others via imitation of emotional expressions. Sample: 39 healthy adults (mean age ~21), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., (PS_AP − (PS_ANg+PS_ANt)/2) − (PL_AP − (PL_ANg+PL_ANt)/2)) with significant clusters and peak coordinates, and cluster-level FWE correction — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptability of coordinates/tables. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore INCLUDE.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study of dynamic social interaction (human vs computer opponent) using a task clearly social in nature. Participants were healthy adults (N=75; age range 18–48), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (cluster-thresholded Z-statistic maps, MNI coordinates reported) and provides coordinates/figures for effects (e.g., dlPFC, dmPFC, TPJ), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Supplementary Methods) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a social ToM task (Frith-Happé) during scanning and includes a healthy comparison group of young adults, so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported one-sample t-tests appear to reflect task-activated regions for the sample or pooled analyses and exploratory whole-brain results are reported for the AN subgroup; no unmasked HC-only whole-brain activation map or HC-specific coordinate table/figure is clearly presented. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting group contrasts/analyses without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive social task (Cyberball) assessing social exclusion (meets I3). The sample consists of 21 healthy adult participants aged 20–37, within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (within-Pla one-sample t tests and paired t tests; uncorrected whole-brain results shown in Tables S3 and S4, and task contrasts described in the text), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-groups-only, participants are within age range, empirical fMRI data are reported). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–32) that used task-based fMRI to compare person-related (social) fact learning with non-social categories and a nonsemantic control. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, ANOVA, cluster-corrected maps) are reported and interpreted for the healthy sample. The task probes perception/understanding of others (social conceptual processing), satisfying the review objective.

This fMRI study investigates audiovisual speech processing (a social-communication task) and includes a healthy adult control group whose demographics are reported. However, the paper does not present a clearly identified, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Results focus on a main effect of congruency across both groups and on group-by-congruency interaction effects rather than reporting a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports interactions/between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus no qualifying I6 application). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (direction-sensitive coding of observed head turns), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 22–38). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (gray-matter–masked) voxelwise analyses and corrected voxel coordinates and maps (FWE-corrected results and exploratory whole-brain analyses), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate an imitation/urge-to-imitate paradigm (a social-cognitive process related to perception/understanding of others and social interaction), includes a healthy adult sample aged 18–25 with results reported for that group, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, SPM8) with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI with an implicit facial-emotion (social) task (I3) and includes a separate healthy adult control group reported separately (I4). Whole-brain results are reported as between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) in tables/figures, satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I6). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or contrast that is explicitly identified as the healthy/control group’s within-group task effect; results are reported primarily as patient versus control contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study probing social-related processing (self- vs. other-produced skin-to-skin touch), meeting the review’s construct scope (Perception and Understanding of Self/Other). Participants are healthy adults (n=54 across studies; ages within 18–65) and results for healthy groups are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (FWE-corrected voxelwise results, tables/figures and supplementary tables cited) for main effects and condition contrasts (other-touch > self-touch, self-touch < 0, etc.). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary material. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, participants in age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (joint attention/theory-of-mind) using a task in which participants viewed an avatar’s gaze to occluded body/place images, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults age 20–31 with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (body>place and place>body contrasts), figures of whole-brain maps, and a table of activation coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI task study probing social auditory processing (listening to one vs. two walkers), clearly addressing social-related processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=12; ages 22–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and statistical maps/coordinate tables for contrasts (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP1 – NOISE1; STEP2 – NOISE2), normalized to Talairach space. Whole-brain contrasts and coordinates are explicitly described for the healthy participant group, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and includes direct task-evoked activations. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social communication/perception: participants performed valence judgments of audiovisual face-and-voice stimuli (non-verbal emotion communication), which clearly maps to Social Communication / Perception of Others (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (mean age ~25; n=14 analyzed), within 18–65 and reported separately (I4). The paper presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain ANOVAs, cluster-level FWE results, tables/figures) and ROI analyses, with coordinates and cluster statistics reported (I5,I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults using two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) that probe social perception/understanding. The sample is healthy adults (n≈120; ages 18–35). The authors report group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (emotion perspective-taking > shape matching; emotion attribution > gender matching) and whole-brain regression analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (FWE and voxelwise thresholds), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supporting methods).

Although the study includes healthy adult control groups, the fMRI task (passive listening to musical cadences) is not a social-related task as required by the review (I3 not met). Additionally, the reported voxelwise whole-brain results focus on pre-post differences and patient-specific increases (patients vs pooled controls) and do not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied and exclusion criterion E4 applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly investigates social communication (perception and evaluation of different laughter types) using task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (contrasts CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU, etc.), with statistical thresholds, cluster corrections, and coordinate results/tables/figures. Whole-brain activation maps and contrasts for the healthy participant group are clearly described and reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The study reports an fMRI task that probes social perception (fearful faces with gaze direction), includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain within-group results for the control group (AVERTED>DIRECT) with statistical maps/figures and corrected voxelwise analyses. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy controls, participants are within 18–65).

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliation/provocation—clearly a social-related process. Participants are healthy adult males (N=15; mean age 22.3), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps, cluster correction, Talairach coordinates, and figures/tables of activation (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group). Reporting format (tables/figures and text) satisfies acceptable evidence. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical work) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Note: sample is small and male-only (limits generalizability) but does not violate inclusion requirements. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=12, mean age 26) that investigates perception and understanding of others’ actions/effort (social-related processing: force perception during action observation). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (SPM whole-brain and SUIT cerebellar analyses) with thresholds, cluster coordinates, figures, and conjunction analyses clearly attributed to the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task: perception/understanding of others), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required for eligibility.

This study is excluded because it does not report task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results in a healthy adult group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the paper reports resting-state fMRI analyses (seed/ROI and connectivity analyses) and effects of intranasal oxytocin in an ASD patient sample, but does not provide any group-level, whole-brain task activation maps from a healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based social-related fMRI paradigm; analyses are resting-state), I4 (no healthy adult group; sample consists of adults with ASD only and healthy controls are not reported), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete and sufficient to make this determination.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social/empathic processing (pictures of one vs two persons; emotional content) — relevant to social-related constructs (I3). Participants are healthy adult males (mean age ~22; inclusion/exclusion of psychiatric disorders ensured), meeting the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). The paper reports multi-subject, whole-brain random-effects ANOVA results with voxelwise activations (FDR thresholds, Talairach coordinates, tables/figures) for task effects (main effects of emotional content and social relation), providing whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps/results clearly described in the text and tables (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and thus is eligible for inclusion.

This empirical fMRI study (n=51 healthy adults, mean age 22.5) directly investigates social processing (perception of others’ dynamic facial expressions). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation contrasts (dynamic facial expressions vs. dynamic mosaics) with appropriate random-effects analyses and FWE-corrected thresholds, with results shown in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps; I6: results clearly reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review’s content criterion for social-related processing (I3). The task is a forward vs backward passive listening paradigm targeting sentential semantic processing in Mandarin Chinese; there is no manipulation or measure of social constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication, self/other perception). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately; n=22, ages 19–35) and I5/I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps/coordinates for the healthy group are reported: forward > backward, thresholded and tabulated). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I3 (social-related task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used task-based fMRI to examine perception of face gender, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (a social-related construct). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 19–42) with group results reported for the healthy sample. Importantly, the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise random-effects analyses (gender-different > gender-same), with cluster-corrected maps and reported activated clusters/coordinates, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. ROI analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (uses fMRI with a social inference task — the Why/How task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, age 18–45, reported separately). However, it does NOT provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The paper reports whole-brain analyses of Group×Stimulus interactions and ROI-based results, and primarily focuses on between-group contrasts and interactions; there is no unmasked, within-healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (only ROI and between-group/interaction maps are presented). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study uses fMRI with a social-related Theory-of-Mind task (I3) and includes a healthy control group of adults within the 18–65 range (I4). However, the paper reports analyses constrained to pre-specified ROI masks and presents primarily between-group contrasts (ALS>HC) without reporting an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails to meet the whole-brain healthy-group evidence requirement (I5). Exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of empathy and perspective-taking (social cognition), meeting the review’s topic. Participants are healthy adults aged 21–31 (N=18), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain) with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and tables/coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented (including conjunction analyses, time-course analyses, and ROI-corrected contrasts), and whole-brain findings are described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study applying a social-cognitive task (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) — satisfying I3. The sample includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=18) matched for age and education — satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group (healthy controls) task-evoked activation results with whole-brain analyses and voxelwise statistics (thresholds reported, coordinates and significant activations in bilateral STS, inferior prefrontal gyrus, fusiform, amygdala), satisfying I5. Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text/tables (and supplementary material), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported, participants are adults, and this is an original empirical fMRI study). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment involving social-related processing (social reputation), meeting the review topic. The sample consists of 28 healthy young adult participants (14 male, 14 female; ages 20–24), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation analyses (thresholds, cluster-level FWE correction, peak voxels in MNI coordinates, and a results table), clearly identified as group-level results from the healthy/control sample. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and a table of activations. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=31 analyzed, ages 19–30) during a social-related action observation task probing inference of others’ effort (perception/understanding of others). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with voxelwise p<0.001 and cluster-level FWE correction (results reported in tables/peaks and conjunction analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Animated Triangles Task) probing mentalizing (Perception/Understanding of Others). It includes a healthy adult control group (N=17, ages matched to patients within 18–30), and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (within-group control activations and cluster-corrected Z maps are described and shown). Reporting of whole-brain results for the healthy group appears in text and figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (theory of mind/intentions), includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) with ages in the 18–65 range, and presents group-level, whole-brain task activation results for the control group (within-group contrasts and tables/figures of coordinates). Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables, figures, coordinates). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This study used resting-state fMRI and connectome-wide (MDMR/seed-based) analyses correlating intrinsic connectivity with emotional intelligence; it did not use a task-based social fMRI paradigm or report any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes a healthy adult group aged 18–45 with results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task) and I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy participants). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked social fMRI in healthy adults.

Study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task probing social/attachment processing (parents viewing own vs. unfamiliar infant videos), includes healthy adult participants aged 22–37, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain GLM contrasts own-infant>standard-infant and voxelwise intersubject correlation maps) reported in the text/results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and participants are within 18–65). Sample size is modest but does not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes Theory of Mind and social cognition. Sample: 20 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.5), meeting the healthy adult inclusion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts and a parametric modulation analysis (family-wise error corrected, voxelwise maps, and peak coordinates are listed), clearly describing whole-brain results for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social task (processing social hierarchy), uses a healthy adult sample (n=72; analyses on 48 social participants; ages within 19–43 and 19–38 in experiments), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (random-effects SPM5, thresholded and FDR-corrected; tables of coordinates and figures). The results are clearly reported for the healthy/control participants (within-group contrasts such as ‘superior > inferior’) and whole-brain maps/coordinate tables are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulated social information (trustworthiness judgments) versus nonsocial information during an n-back task. Participants were healthy adults (mean age 22; final imaging N=14), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4), clearly identifying healthy-group task effects. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI social-task data, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task activation reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, non-healthy-only groups, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a social-referential paradigm (Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task) that probes self vs other processing (social-related processing). The sample comprises 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 with psychiatric history exclusion criteria, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (SPM8 analyses) with group contrasts, tables of clusters, and voxelwise figures (e.g., Figure 2) clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a social-related task (facial emotion discrimination) addressing perception/understanding of others, enrolled healthy adult participants (control group ages 19–35), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (within-group contrasts for the normal control group and clusters/tables of whole-brain results with FWE-corrected thresholds). Whole-brain results are presented in tables and described in the text (not ROI-only), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines facial emotion recognition (a social-communication/perception task) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain results, but the reported whole-brain maps are presented as between-group (LDA > HDA and HDA > LDA) contrasts between two healthy subgroups. The paper does not present an unmasked, within-group or main-effect whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group independent of between-group contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (explicit and implicit processing of emotional facial expressions), satisfying the review topic. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7 yrs) reported separately alongside a clinical group. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain task analyses with cluster coordinates and descriptions of activations attributable to controls (e.g., control-specific activation of left cerebellum and left amygdalohippocampal region; main effects and diagnosis × experiment interactions reported in tables and text). Results are reported as group-level whole-brain contrasts/coordinates (not ROI-only). The full-text is complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI to study prosodic speech processing, a social-communication construct; (I4) includes a healthy adult control group (8 males, age ~23) reported separately; (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps for the control group (one-sample t-tests, activation and deactivation maps with FDR correction); (I6) whole-brain results are described in text and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small and one clinical group is also present, control-group whole-brain results are clearly reported, so the study is eligible for inclusion.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adult participants (12 adults aged 21–28). Methods describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise contrasts (cooperation vs independent, competition vs independent, and direct contrasts), reported in tables and figures. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines perception of emotional (fearful vs neutral) body actions, a social-related task (perception and understanding of others). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (12 adult males) reported separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (e.g., Fearful vs Neutral; Dynamic vs Static) for the control/healthy group with tables, figures, and thresholded statistical maps described in the text. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social communication and intention understanding in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 24), using a task with communicative vs private actions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholding, conjunction and PPI results, and tables/figures describing activations. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and figures provided). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met.

Provided ‘full text’ is a cookie/privacy preference page only; core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not present. Unable to verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (presence and reporting of a healthy adult group 18–65), and I5/I6 (reporting of group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps). No exclusion criteria can be positively identified from the truncated content. Exclude pending retrieval of the full article; recommend obtaining the full text to reassess eligibility.

This fMRI study investigates impression formation (perception and understanding of others), uses a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (20 males, ages 19–31), and reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA with results shown in table/figures). Thus it meets the review objective and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial decisions (family assistance), a clear social-related task (mentalizing, affiliation/attachment). Sample consists of 25 healthy young adults (Mage=20.2), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and corrected inference, and whole-brain regression and PPI analyses; results are reported for the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, age 18–26) that explicitly investigates emotion perception/evaluation from vocalizations and music and relates these processes to medial prefrontal regions involved in social cognition (e.g., theory of mind/empathy). The study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain group-level analyses (contrasts, conjunctions, cluster correction) and reports results in text, figures, and tables (including coordinates). The social-related construct (perception and understanding of others’ emotions/social cognition) is clearly targeted by the emotion-tracking task. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition (evaluating whether one person’s actions are consistent with another’s intentions) using a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (final N=16, ages 18–29). The manuscript reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise ANOVAs) and ROI analyses, and describes significant whole-brain effects (e.g., medial prefrontal, visual, and somatosensory regions) with statistical thresholds and coordinates. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked results clearly identified for the healthy sample. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related facial emotion recognition task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~23.6) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper provides group-level whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain clusters/coordinates for the healthy control group (e.g., NTOXT>PLA clusters in inferior frontal gyrus and fusiform gyrus), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets I5). Whole-brain results are reported in the text and tables (meets I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (perception of active listening), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=22 recruited; N=18 analyzed; mean age ~21.7 years). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests on contrasts: with active listening > control; without active listening > control; with active listening > without active listening) with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds and reports significant clusters and beta values. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=17, ages 23–39) using a social-related task (observation of another’s hand being touched — perception/understanding of others). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps and coordinates; contrasts touch observation > control, masked with real touch), clearly from the healthy sample. The paper includes complete methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults (native Japanese speakers, ages 19–31) that used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses to report task-evoked activation maps. The experimental tasks explicitly probe social communication (communicative vs descriptive speech) satisfying the review’s social-related construct. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects analyses and interaction and main-effect contrasts (with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates communicative (social) speech production versus description, directly addressing social communication processes. Sample: healthy adult native Japanese speakers (n=30, ages 19–31), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., ECOM–EOBJ, L2COM vs L1COM, interaction (L2COM–L2DES)–(L1COM–L1DES)) with tables of peak coordinates and cluster-corrected maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Whole article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, healthy adult group results reported separately). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (perception/understanding of others’ gaze/theory-of-mind). It reports data from 32 healthy adult participants aged 18–52. The authors performed a whole-brain, voxelwise (searchlight) group-level analysis and report group-level decoding maps, peak coordinates, and a whole-brain significant voxel (right TPJ) with correction procedures described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and materials, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory interpersonal touch (a clearly social-related task) in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (e.g., Target, Modality, Target×Modality interactions) with cluster-level correction, figures, and a table of coordinates; analyses include conjunctions and voxel-wise results within a tactile localizer mask. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to a subgroup). The study is empirical and not ROI-only, resting-state, or between-group-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (face-to-face joint attention) including healthy adult control groups. Neurotypical adults (matched control n=13, ROI control n=22; ages 18–39) are reported separately. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and reports voxelwise contrasts (e.g., RJA vs SA, IJA vs SA) with thresholded maps and coordinate tables for the neurotypical groups. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) social fMRI task, (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately, (I5) whole-brain group-level task activation maps from healthy/control groups, and (I6) acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in a sample of healthy participants, reporting group-level whole-brain task activation results (cluster-corrected maps and coordinates). The sample consists of young healthy adults (mean age 21.4; range 16.9–25.7) — while the lower bound includes one participant under 18, the study reports a single healthy group with adults in the 18–65 range and provides group-level whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (repeated public good game probing social tie formation/other-regarding preferences). Scanned sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=25 analyzed; mean age ~22.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FSL GLM, cluster-wise FWE correction) with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception/attribution of animacy/mental states to moving shapes), conducted in healthy adult participants (15 males, mean age 26.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations. Therefore it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range). Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

Although the study used task-based fMRI of social/affective face processing (I3) and included a healthy adult control group (age 18–65) reported separately (I4), the full text presents mainly between-group interaction and patient-vs-control comparisons rather than an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The Methods state one-sample and two-sample t-tests were conducted, but the Results focus on group differences and ROI analyses; no whole-brain TD within-group statistical map (or coordinates/figure/table unambiguously reporting a healthy-group task effect) is reported in the provided text. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study does not satisfy I5 and must be excluded.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (modified Trust Game) directly probing reciprocity/trust (social-related processing). The sample comprised healthy adult participants aged 18–30 (reported group-level results for the healthy sample). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (GLM one-sample/t-tests with cluster correction) and provides tables/figures of activation coordinates. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures satisfies the meta-analysis reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-adult sample) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the study uses resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for a healthy adult group) and E5 (participants are adolescents aged 11–18, outside the 18–65 adult range; no separate healthy adult subgroup is reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use task-based fMRI; it uses resting-state fcMRI), I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65; the control group are adolescents), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control adult group), I6 (not applicable because no task whole-brain results are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample and examines social processing (emotion recognition) under chemosensory stimuli, so it meets I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the analyses and reported results are restricted to a priori ROI-based voxelwise tests (amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, OFC, FFA) with results corrected within ROIs; the paper does not present unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps or whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E2.

This fMRI study investigates implicit facial emotion processing (a social perception task) and includes a healthy control (HC) group. The full text reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the HC group (one-sample t-tests, SPM8, cluster-wise thresholds) and provides group-level results and coordinates. The HC group is described as age-matched healthy adults and reported separately from clinical/high-risk participants. The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content present).
