Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a social-related fMRI task, presence of a healthy adult group with separately reported whole-brain task maps, and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining attachment-related processing using masked facial emotions (socially relevant task: affiliation/attachment). Sample = 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (main effects of masked sad/happy faces and regression correlations with attachment avoidance) with coordinates and corrected thresholds (tables/figures). All required whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

The study reports an fMRI experiment of an explicitly social/affiliative task (anticipation and performance of romantic caress), recruiting healthy adult participants (ages 19–34 in 12 couples). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise task-evoked analyses are reported (no-touch and touch contrasts, direct contrasts, whole-brain covariance with Passionate Love Scale, conjunction analyses), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are presented in text/tables/figures and methods/results/discussion are included in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of faces vs objects) and includes a healthy adult sample (21 adults age 18–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (faces>objects) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates (Table 3) describing whole-brain effects and regression of activation against age; FFA group metrics are reported separately for adults in Table 2. Whole-brain results are reported for the healthy sample and provided in figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (social reflection: Self and Other judgments vs affect labeling), satisfying I3. The sample consists of 22 healthy adult participants (mean age 37.4, range within 18–65) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (cortical surface–based) task-evoked activation for the SR>AL contrast, with cluster-corrected results, figures (e.g., Fig.1B) and tables (Table 2) documenting voxel/vertex-wise effects from the healthy sample, meeting I5 and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study qualifies for inclusion.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment of social communication (emotional prosody production with a social interaction/feedback condition), includes healthy adult participants (final N=23, ages 20–33), and presents group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (within-group contrasts, voxelwise maps thresholded and described in text/figures). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported (main effects and condition contrasts). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This paper reports an fMRI study of social appraisal (preference judgments of faces), meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=21) recruited to match the patient group and reports results for the healthy group separately (within-group contrasts and descriptions). Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate tables for the PREF>GENDER contrasts are presented for groups (figures and tables explicitly display/control group activations and PPI results for controls). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or out-of-range age/sample-only reporting). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that reports whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinates for the healthy control group separately. The Methods and Results provide group-level, voxelwise contrasts for controls (e.g., approachability > gender) with cluster-corrected statistics and peak MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Healthy adult control sample (n=24) is described and analyzed separately. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI during a clearly social-related task (strategic decisions involving human vs computer partners and mentalizing about others), uses a healthy adult sample (47 right-handed male students, ages in 18–65 range), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (GLM whole-brain analyses with FSL randomise TFCE and familywise error correction; vmPFC and other whole-brain corrected effects reported). Results are presented for the healthy/control group and whole-brain effects are reported in the main text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a social motor response (social inclusion/exclusion) task and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in healthy adult participants. The sample consists of 18 healthy adults (mean age 42 ± 12), satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects analyses with FDR whole-brain correction and displays tables/figures of activations (e.g., dorsal anterior cingulate, frontal operculum, ventral striatum), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (Cyberball social exclusion), with healthy adult participants (Chinese university students, final N=42; screened for neurological history). It presents whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) across all participants and separate within-group whole-brain analyses, with results reported in text, tables, and figures (P<0.05 FWE). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–20) examining trait empathy and neural responses during music listening, which is framed as social-related processing (perception/understanding of others and social cognition). The paper presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and reports activation coordinates and figures for the healthy participant groups in both experiments. Methods, results, and discussion are complete in the full text provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (second-order Theory of Mind) task during BOLD fMRI (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=25, ages 18–60) with results reported separately alongside the bipolar group (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures of activations) and describes within-group activation patterns for controls (meets I5). Whole-brain results are presented in text, tables, and figures (acceptable per I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

Excluded because exclusion criterion E5 is met: the sample includes participants older than 65 (up to age 68) and the authors do not report a separate analysis restricted to a healthy adult subgroup within 18–65. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps/analyses with voxelwise results and coordinates) and I6 (whole-brain results are presented in figures/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample does not conform to age 18–65 without a separately reported subgroup), and I3 (task is word/pseudoword repetition for probing speech production/aging; it is not a clear social-related task or explicit social-communication paradigm). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

Exclusion E2 met: the reported neuroimaging results are based on a priori ROI analyses with FWE correction performed within ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported in this full text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — physician–patient interaction, empathy/compassion) and I4 (healthy adult physician sample, ages 25–37). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map from the healthy group is presented). The full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI task investigating social decision-making modulated by perceived gaze direction in a healthy adult sample. Participants: healthy adults (n=27 final; ages 20–29) meeting the age/sample criterion. The task is social-related (prosocial vs selfish choices toward human vs robot counterparts; perception/understanding of others). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results are reported (flexible factorial model; voxel-wise p<0.001 with FWE cluster correction across the whole brain and ROI small-volume corrections), with coordinates and cluster statistics provided. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, healthy adult group reported separately).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (Narrative Experiment: N=41, ages 18–37; separate localizer group N=14). The task is social-related (empathy/Theory of Mind narratives and pain/localizer tasks). The paper includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (SnPM, corrected p<0.05), contrasts for pain vs control and condition-specific contrasts, and reports peak coordinates (Table 3) and whole-brain figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text (not truncated). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=40 behavioral, n=34 fMRI; ages 19.5–32.7) that used task-based fMRI during a social task (trust game with partner pupil manipulations). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (whole-brain GLM results, cluster thresholds, coordinates, and ROI analyses) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21) using a social cognition task (viewing others in pain — perception/understanding of others/empathy). The manuscript includes whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (pre-priming whole-brain FDR-corrected maps; post-priming whole-brain results reported) and provides coordinates/tables and ROI analyses. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are described and reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion(s) met: E2. Inclusion(s) met: I3, I4. Inclusion(s) not met: I5. The paper reports an fMRI visual perspective-taking task (social cognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3, I4). However, the Methods state that second-level activation analyses were restricted to predefined prefrontal ROIs and results are reported within these ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map or healthy-group whole-brain contrast/coordinate table is reported for the healthy/control group. Although exploratory whole-brain functional connectivity was performed, this does not satisfy the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5 and meeting exclusion criterion E2.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives) in healthy adults (ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frames, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with coordinate tables/figures and thresholding procedures. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (joint Simon task manipulating belief about a human vs. computer co-actor), addressing perception/understanding of others and self-other processing. The sample is 36 healthy adults aged 20–30 (within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (GLM, random-effects group analysis) with corrected thresholds (alphasim, p<0.005, cluster size >20) and presents contrasts and coordinates in figures/tables. Whole-brain congruency and condition effects are clearly described for the healthy participant group. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attitude/preference change toward others after political advertisements), using task-based fMRI during a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults aged 18–27 (N=40). The paper reports group-level random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM t-maps), with reported coordinates, tables, and figures identifying activation clusters in prefrontal and reward-related regions. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social processes), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported via coordinates/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult nulliparous women (ages 19–29) using social-related tasks (perception of infant cries and faces), thus addressing social processing (Perception/Understanding of Others; affiliation/attachment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., cry vs pink noise; happy vs neutral faces) with corrected whole-brain thresholds and displays coordinates and brain maps. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical fMRI data reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of reactive social aggression using a social interaction task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) with human opponents, probing perception/understanding of others and social decision-making. Sample: healthy adults (n=15 analyzed; mean age ~22.9), within 18–65. Methods report whole-brain random-effects, voxelwise GLM analyses and report group-level activation maps and stereotaxic coordinates (tables/figures) for decision and outcome contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, pediatric/older-only sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test, a social-cognitive task probing perception/understanding of others; (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16, mean age 20.8) reported separately; (I5) The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (emotion vs control) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and listed peak coordinates (Tables/Figures); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

E3 met: The study reports resting-state intrinsic connectivity (seed/network analyses) and PET-derived dopamine responses during mother–infant film viewing, but it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked fMRI activation map for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes healthy adult mothers, ages 21–42, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-evoked fMRI whole-brain analysis reported — fMRI results are intrinsic/resting-state connectivity rather than task activation), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is provided), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain task results reported in text/figures/tables). Full text appears complete (full methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded for this meta-analysis because it reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and PET outcomes without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map.

This study reports task-based functional MRI of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adults (ages 18–32). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., faces associated with behaviors vs. novel faces; negative vs. positive; disgust vs. aggression) with Talairach coordinates, cluster volumes, and statistical thresholds reported in tables and figures. Results for the healthy/control sample are reported separately and not limited to ROIs; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study directly examining neural correlates of persuasion—a social-cognitive/mentalizing process—during task performance. Participants are healthy adults (American and Korean samples; ages reported within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (persuasive > unpersuasive) with thresholding and tables of coordinates (Tables 1A, 2, 4) and figures, clearly identified for healthy/control groups. Although ROI analyses were also performed in Study 3, whole-brain task-evoked results are reported for the healthy samples. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that used whole-brain, voxelwise analyses of BOLD responses during an emotional prosody and lexico-semantic emotion working-memory task (a social communication task involving perception/identification of others’ emotions). Sample: 26 healthy right-handed adult participants (mean age 21.2), satisfying healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain parametric analyses and provides tables of coordinates and figures (Tables 2–4, Fig.1) describing voxelwise activations for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present, so fulltext is complete.

This study uses task-based fMRI during free viewing of a college basketball game that explicitly targets social-related processing (self-relevance, social context, and social cognition for fans), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (male fans, mean ages 20–22), satisfying the age/healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked GLM results (voxelwise maps, statistical thresholds, and coordinate tables) and ICA results; whole-brain SPM contrasts and coordinates are presented in the text/tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting criteria. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures is present. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy participant maps, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (direct and reflected self-appraisals; perception/understanding of self and others) and includes a healthy adult sample (N=12, ages 22.6–30.4). The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, conjunctions, between- and within-group contrasts) clearly identified for the adult group, with reported coordinates, thresholds, and correction procedures. Adult results are reported separately from the adolescent sample. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of Theory-of-Mind/false-belief reasoning (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others). It includes a separately reported healthy neurotypical adult group (N=15, mean age ~29.9) and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses for the control (NT) group (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain SPMs, cluster- and FWE-corrected results, and tables/figures of significant clusters). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation using a one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma (social task) with whole-brain task-based analyses reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: PD game/cooperation), I4 (healthy adult sample; final analyzed N=18, mean age 21.04, within 18–65), I5 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses reported with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables/contrast descriptions). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not an only between-group contrast, participants within age range, and this is empirical data. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental XLSX references do not prevent treating the core article as complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (inferring others’ intentions/means), includes a healthy adult control group (22 TD young adults reported separately), and presents whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group (within-group maps and between-group contrasts reported and thresholded; coordinates/figures/tables described). Full-text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used the False-Belief Localizer (a social theory-of-mind task) during task fMRI (meets I3). It reports data from healthy adult control groups (Caltech: n=18, ages 21–46; MIT: n=462, ages 18–69), with healthy-group results reported separately (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrast maps and whole-brain analyses for the healthy reference groups (e.g., MIT whole-brain results and Fig. 2), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Consequently, the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates social processing (emotional face perception) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the fMRI results are reported using an a priori amygdala ROI with statistical correction within that ROI and the reported group-level results focus on ROI activations. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain coordinates/tables or whole-brain figures for the control group are reported). Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map for healthy group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze perception) meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (separate analyses reported). Voxelwise task contrasts are reported and described for the control group (e.g., controls direct gaze > averted gaze) with coordinates and figures/tables; whole-brain contrasts (faces vs. null) are referenced as FWE-corrected at the whole-brain level. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social persuasion (celebrity ‘expert power’) using a social-related task (celebrity–object pairs) with healthy adult participants (young females, mean age 21.8). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects task-evoked activation analyses (thresholds, cluster correction) and lists activation clusters in tables/figures (whole-brain maps and ROI small-volume follow-ups). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-related face-processing task and included a healthy adult control group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper reports a whole-group (AS + NT) faces>houses whole-brain map (Table 1) and reports group-comparison contrasts (NT>AS) and ROI analyses of the amygdala for the control group, but no standalone, voxelwise whole-brain faces>houses (or equivalent) statistical map for the healthy/control group is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions; disgust perception), with healthy adult participants (mean age ~21). The paper reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA, thresholding, reported significant clusters and tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses fMRI to examine neural responses during music appreciation and explicitly interprets activations in default mode/ToM and cognitive-empathy regions as reflecting social-cognitive engagement for artistic music (i.e., perception/understanding of others/social cognition). It reports healthy adult participants (18–24 years) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction, with coordinates provided. Thus it meets the review objective of social-related processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive social (mentalizing) paradigm (Prisoner’s Dilemma) addressing attachment/social cognition. Sample: 164 healthy adult participants (age range 19–35) with results reported for the healthy group. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (contrast task > control) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; activation peaks/coordinates and clusters are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening.

This study uses task-based fMRI during clearly social tasks (empathy-eliciting campaign videos and an interactive hyperscanning social game), meeting I3. The sample includes healthy adult participants (Control Drivers: males mean age 34.9, within 18–65; Rehabilitated Drivers are non-clinical and reported separately), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (GLM, FLAME, non-parametric correction) and presents whole-brain z-maps/clusters for contrasts involving the control group (e.g., campaign>control and CD>RD), satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are described in text and figures/tables (thresholded maps and cluster tables), meeting I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: analyses are whole-brain task-evoked activations (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported).

This fMRI study investigates emotion recognition (a social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I3 and I4). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; results are reported primarily as between-group contrasts, interactions, ROI analyses, and post-hoc group comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy-for-pain (a social-related task) in adult participants including a healthy control group (ages 22–63). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., High Pain–Low Pain in Other, masked with Self) with coordinates and z-scores (reported in main text and Supplementary Table 1) and performs second-level random-effects analyses; results for control/healthy participants are reported separately. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full, and whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) directly probing social cognition and trust, addressing the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6, range consistent with 18–65) with group-level analyses reported for the healthy sample. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results (group contrasts, interaction effects) with cluster-size correction and provide tables/figures and peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results for the healthy groups (prosocial vs proself) are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study is an auditory attention/motion-detection task (identifying direction of crossing footsteps) in healthy adult participants (ages 20–29) and uses whole-brain, random-effects GLM contrasts (‘footstep minus rest’) reported at group level (maps in supplementary material) and subsequent connectivity analyses. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample) and I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map). It also satisfies I6 (whole-brain results presented in supplementary figures/tables). However, the task is not a social-related task targeting constructs such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of self/others—the paradigm manipulates auditory attention to motion and does not probe social processing. Therefore it fails I3 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study investigates humor processing—a social cognitive/emotional process involving perception and understanding of others (ToM/ social cognition). It used task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) reporting group-level contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral, parametric modulation) with corrected statistics and conjunctions, and provides tables/figures of results. The sample comprises 29 healthy adult participants (mean age 27, range within 18–65). Reporting includes whole-brain maps/coordinates. Therefore it satisfies the review’s task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This fMRI study uses a social-context decision task (SCDT) involving peer presence and examines counterfactual emotions (regret, relief, disappointment, elation), meeting the review’s social-processing scope. The sample includes a healthy adult group (young adults, age 21–22) reported separately alongside adolescents. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-sample and age-group second-level GLM contrasts) with cluster tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results. Reporting of coordinates, clusters, and figures is present. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22, ages 21–52) using a social cognition task (modified Reading-the-Mind-in-the-Eyes Test) directly assessing perception/understanding of others. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (whole-brain contrasts, statistical parametric maps, and coordinate tables with MNI coordinates and corrected thresholds) clearly pertaining to the healthy adult sample. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for this review (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/influence in healthy adult participants (mean age ~20.6). The task involved social processing (message encoding/intention to recommend) and used task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported at the group level (whole-brain results with MNI coordinates and thresholding are provided). Thus it meets the review’s neuroimaging and sample requirements and reports whole-brain activation maps rather than ROI- or connectivity-only results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognitive processing using mindreading tasks (RMET and the newly developed NCET), conducted in a healthy adult sample (N=38, mean age 24.1). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., MIND>SEX; interaction (WC–NWC)*(CM–AM)) with cluster- and peak-level results and FWE correction, and describes these maps in the text and tables. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in main text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (N=21 healthy adult males, ages 23–33) viewed and rated dyadic nonverbal interactions during task-based fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects flexible factorial ANOVA) with contrasts and cluster-level corrected results and coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Core article content (introduction, detailed methods, behavioral and fMRI results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (explicit mental simulation of others’ actions/feelings) in healthy adults (20 participants, ages 21–47), and it provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (GLM SPM-t maps, cluster-level FDR-corrected) and corresponding figures/tables. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling verification of measures and analyses. Although the paper also reports connectivity (ISPS/SBPS), it additionally includes conventional whole-brain activation analyses, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate self-recognition (a social-cognition construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), with a healthy adult sample (n≈35, ages 18–24). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (SPM5; contrasts, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with tables of coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult or clinical-only sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (N=20, healthy adults aged 18–27) performed a task eliciting thoughts about others’ mental states (mentalizing), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (searchlight MVPA, network-level analyses, one-sample random-effects t tests, whole-brain univariate maps, cluster correction via Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and presents tables/figures and supplementary tables of results, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

Full text provides empirical fMRI data using an explicit social Theory-of-Mind (false belief) task (Belief vs Photo) — a social-related construct (Perception and Understanding of Others). Healthy control group of neurotypical adults is reported separately (N=462; ages include 18–69, with the sample clearly including adults within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Belief>Photo) for the NT group, with corrected results, figures, and cluster tables described in the text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults aged 18–41 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task analyses (ANOVA, contrasts vs baseline, conjunctions) with thresholding and FWE-corrected results and figures/tables, and describes these whole-brain results in the text (meets whole-brain reporting criterion). Clinical scales are ancillary and healthy-group results are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This fMRI study used the Ultimatum Game, a social interaction task probing fairness (social decision-making). It recruited healthy adult participants (n=28; mean age 25.1), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (GLM, second-level random-effects ANOVA) with voxelwise and clusterwise thresholds and provides tables of coordinates and statistical maps/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This study used task-based fMRI (cyberball) to probe social interaction/rejection (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (20 female HCs) reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial and t-contrasts) and describes condition and within-group effects for HCs (post-hoc within-group effects and t-contrasts referenced in Supplementary Table S4), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group (meets I5). Results are reported in the main text and supplementary materials (tables/figures), consistent with I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests social interaction (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=30, mean age 21.2). The task probes social cooperation/defection (clearly a social-related construct). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests, voxelwise thresholding p<.001, spatial extent thresholds) and whole-brain voxelwise exploratory correlations for the healthy sample, with results presented in text, figures, and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=26, ages 18–35) using social-related tasks assessing perception/understanding of others (communicative intent). Whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise analyses are reported (second-level t-tests; threshold P<0.001 uncorrected, cluster k>10) with peak coordinates and cluster statistics. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI of face processing (a social-related task) and includes healthy adult participants, and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however, the paper does not present a clear group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The main whole-brain analyses appear to be conducted on a combined sample of patients and controls, and the independent (healthy-only) replication used an anatomical ROI approach rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain result). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) strictly apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making using an interactive coin-distribution task (social-related processing), collected in healthy adult participants (N=27; mean age 21.25; screened for psychiatric/neurological history). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (SPM8; whole-brain t-contrasts, FWE cluster correction, coordinates/clusters reported) for multiple conditions (Friend, Disliked Peer, Unfamiliar, etc.), with results presented in text/tables and figures. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during moral reasoning (a social-cognition task), includes a healthy adult control group (N=28, ages 18–55) with results reported separately, and provides group-level, whole-brain one-sample analyses for the healthy control group (Moral vs BL) with FWE-corrected maps/tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI experiment explicitly probing social perception (judging facing-toward vs away of point-light and human-like walkers), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (ANOVAs, contrasts) with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding (p<0.05 FWE) and tables/figures of activation; thus whole-brain evidence is available and reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 26; n=18 analyzed) that uses task-based fMRI during social interaction tasks (stag-hunt and entry games). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and surviving cluster-level FWE correction, and provides MNI coordinates and statistical maps/cluster reports. The tasks probe social-related constructs (strategic uncertainty, understanding others’ choices), satisfying the review’s social-processing scope. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses task-based paradigms probing social processing (take advice game and trust game) with fMRI acquisition and analyses. The sample consists of 31 healthy adult participants (age 24.3±3.8), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked results (searchlight MVPA and whole-brain univariate contrasts) clearly identified as group-level effects for the healthy participant group, with cluster- and voxel-level corrected maps and tables described in the text and supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, neuroimaging acquisition and preprocessing, and statistical analyses, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing: participants watched actors grasping objects in angry/joyful social contexts (social perception/understanding of others). Sample: twenty healthy adults (ages 23–33) with healthy-group results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (GLM, ANOVA) with whole-brain FWE-corrected maps and tables of coordinates (Tables 2–3) clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain maps, not a non-empirical paper, and participants within age range). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (direct vs. averted gaze) and includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (meets I3, I4). However, this manuscript reports psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity (task-modulated connectivity) analyses rather than univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group. The reported "whole-brain" results refer to PPI connectivity maps, not standard task activation contrasts. Therefore it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Per exclusion criterion E3 (seed-based connectivity only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), the paper must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (a social cognition task). It includes a healthy control group of adults (age-matched controls, n=13) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results (within-group activations and coordinates, Table 3; figures show whole-brain statistical maps for contrasts such as ToM vs Physical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=73, age 18–22) that used fMRI while participants viewed social versus nonsocial scenes (a social-related task addressing perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (social > nonsocial contrast) with voxelwise thresholding and describes whole-brain results and ROI supplemental analyses. Thus it provides healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (social reasoning/theory-of-mind and emotion understanding) in healthy adult participants (N=45; ages 19-23). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects results, multiple-comparison correction, peak coordinates in Appendix A, and whole-brain maps/figures), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Results for social tasks are clearly described and contrasted with mechanical tasks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this fMRI study investigates social-related processing (personal familiarity/close relatives) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy control group, it explicitly studies ‘healthy elderly’ participants. The manuscript does not report a healthy adult sample within the required age range (18–65). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only participants outside the 18–65 range with no qualifying healthy subgroup). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described). Inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample age 18–65) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) and reports neural correlates, but the sample consists of adolescents across three developmental phases rather than healthy adults (18–65). No subgroup of healthy adults is reported separately. Therefore it fails the sample inclusion criterion (I4) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (participants only outside the 18–65 range).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) (I3); the sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range with group-level results reported separately for the healthy participants (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and cluster-corrected maps and tables of coordinates for contrasts (social exclusion > fair play, same- vs other-gender exclusion) (I5); results are presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), it is not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within the age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=25 females, mean age 23.2). Participants performed a social (mentalizing) task about friends and kin during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (friend > kin contrast and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholding, tables of clusters/coordinates, and figures. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears to be a complete full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from healthy group), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial (social) learning in healthy adults. It meets I3: uses task-based fMRI targeting social/prosocial processing; I4: sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–32) with results reported for the healthy group; I5: reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and peak coordinates (with voxelwise/FWE/SVC results and tables/figures); I6: whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, tables, and figures (including supplemental tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study uses fMRI with a social face-processing task (fearful faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=19, age ~32), it does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map from the healthy/control group alone. The paper mainly reports group results across all participants and between-group contrasts (controls vs TLE) and ROI-based percent signal change for controls. Because there is no clearly identified whole-brain, within-group healthy-control task map (unmasked) presented, it fails exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore it must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social perception (observation of touch to another’s hand), uses healthy adult participants (mean age 26, 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE-corrected results, tables, figures, and MNI coordinates. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (modified Cyberball) probing social-evaluative exclusion — directly relevant to social processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (20 men, 20 women; mean age 27.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., EX>IN, PG EX>FG IN) with voxelwise FWE correction and provides tables of peak coordinates and cluster sizes. Whole-brain results are clearly presented in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task activation maps).

This empirical fMRI study used task-based fMRI with socially relevant, attachment-related stimuli (own-infant and mother–infant interaction videos). Participants were healthy adult mothers aged 22–37 (N=23 analyzed), meeting the adult healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with statistical maps and tables described in the text and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=21 analyzed, mean age ~23.7), using a task involving emotional facial expressions during ToM judgments. The paper reports group-level, within-subject whole-brain task contrasts (EFE > no EFE and whole-brain tables/figures and ROI analyses) clearly identified from the healthy/control sample. Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in the text. Thus it satisfies the fMRI social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (tables/figures) meeting inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range age) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective task (threat-of-shock while holding a friend, stranger, or alone) that directly probes social regulation of neural threat responding, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 23.6), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses used to identify functional ROIs (cluster-wise tests with FSL, Z-threshold and cluster p-threshold) and provides ROI coordinates and statistical results (Table 1 and text), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, are not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the article is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining integration of speaker characteristics (a social-communication/self-other inference process) during auditory sentence comprehension. It includes a separate healthy control group of adults (age 18–39) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts for the control group (with coordinates, figures and tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, adult sample within range, empirical data present).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — all participants are older adults (final sample N=14, mean age ~71.7 years), i.e., outside the required 18–65 age range, and no healthy adult subgroup within 18–65 is reported. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — study used fMRI during a social-related task (perception/understanding of others; participants judged affect from social target videos); I5 — whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported (behavioral PLS, seed PLS, clusters and coordinates); I6 — whole-brain results are described and reported in text/tables. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — sample does not include healthy adults within 18–65 and no separate analysis of such a subgroup is provided. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing the age-based inclusion criterion (E5). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (facial emotion and age judgments invoking social cognition/Perception and Understanding of Others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=27; ages 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results. The Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FSL Randomise nonparametric testing) and the Results present within-group and between-group whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables (e.g., within-group activation maps, Tables/Figures for controls and overall sample). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported; participants are within age range; empirical task fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) during BOLD fMRI, reporting results from healthy adult participants (final sample N=22, ages 18–29) and explicitly conducting whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Exclusion > Inclusion) and a smell×condition interaction with tables/figures and Monte Carlo cluster correction. Whole-brain results are described in text and VOI follow-ups are supplementary to these whole-brain findings. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (social reward/punishment) meeting the review focus on social processing. Sample: 28 healthy adult women aged 20–42, reported separately from clinical subgroups, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (an uncorrected whole-brain exploration at p<.001 and reported coordinates/observations outside the VTA, including nucleus accumbens), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (personal familiarity/identification of close relatives and familiar places), satisfying the social constructs of affiliation/attachment and perception of others/self. It reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (familiar>unfamiliar) with SPM maps and cluster-level correction, and presents within-group results for healthy young and elderly participants. At least one healthy adult group (young participants) falls within the 18–65 range, and the sample is described as cognitively healthy. Results are reported as whole-brain maps/coordinates (figures and tables) consistent with inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age-appropriate healthy group reported, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion met: E4 — the imaging results presented are predominantly between-group contrasts (schizophrenia vs control) and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or clearly identified voxelwise group-level statistical map for the healthy/control group alone. Figures and tables report between-group clusters and percent signal change by group, but no whole-brain healthy-group map or coordinate-based within-group healthy activation results are reported as a primary, unmasked healthy-group task effect. (b) Inclusion met: I3 — fMRI was used during a social-related (cognitive empathy/emotional perspective-taking) task; I4 — a healthy adult control group (n=24; ages 18–50) is included and reported separately. (c) Inclusion not met: I5 — no clear whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map is reported. I6 is therefore not satisfied because qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results are not present in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because I5 is not met and E4 applies, the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (self/other evaluation with perspective-taking) and includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group; however, the full text presents combined-group whole-brain contrasts and between-group comparisons and ROI analyses, but does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it fails to meet I5. Exclusion is based on E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts/interaction and combined-group maps without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing dynamic facial emotional expressions) in healthy adult participants (fMRI N=40, mean age 30.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (dynamic > static) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of coordinates and describes the second-level one-sample t-test results, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures descriptions) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults 18–65).

The full text reports an fMRI experiment using social/empathy-induction traffic-awareness videos (social-related task). Sample: 20 healthy adult males (ages 20–28), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (CV>NV) with FWE correction (p<0.05) and peak coordinates/tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This study used task-based fMRI to examine human perception of affective vocalisations (social communication/perception of others), matching the review’s social-related constructs. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 25.9) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., species contrast human > chimpanzee > macaque) with MNI coordinates, tables and figures (p < .001 uncorrected), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension—a social-communication task involving perception/understanding of others’ emotions—so it addresses the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–51), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (e.g., emotional vs. neutral, complex vs. simple contrasts) with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates. Thus whole-brain healthy-group task effects are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-group-only contrast, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind/social exchange) in healthy adults. The sample analyzed comprises healthy adults (N=12, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (story and card contrasts) using SPM2 and a group random-effects model, with tables and figures of activated clusters and coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly described and contrasted (social contract, precaution, descriptive) for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the paper reports between-group contrasts (controls > schizophrenia) and pooled/main effects but does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map identified as coming from the healthy/control group in the provided full text. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses fMRI during a social-related task (irony comprehension/social communication); I4 — includes a healthy adult control group reported separately alongside patients. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the manuscript as provided does not clearly report at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly labelled as the healthy/control group (results for the control group are only referenced as previously published, and within-paper results emphasize between-group contrasts). I6 not applicable because no clear healthy-group whole-brain map is included in text/tables/supplementary material presented here. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (core article content present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain activation map, triggering E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, ages 45–62) using a social-affective task (viewing film clips of people in distress) with explicit emotion-regulation conditions (Compassion, Reappraisal). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative, Reappraisal > Watch-Negative), with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures describing results for the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article reports an fMRI task probing visuo-social perception (faces/occiputs), satisfying the social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult human sample (n=30; age range 21–50) reported separately from the canine sample. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results and contrasts for the healthy human group (GLM contrasts, thresholding, cluster correction, figures and peak coordinates). Results are clearly described in the main text (complete intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing with whole-brain analyses and reports group-level voxelwise results (tables/figures), satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, participant groups fall outside the review age range: the younger group includes participants aged 17–27 (includes minors <18) and the older group is 65–75 (entirely >65). No group is reported that is exclusively within the target 18–65 age range, nor is a healthy adult subgroup (18–65) analyzed separately. Therefore the study violates the age-range eligibility and meets exclusion criterion E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-perception task (passive viewing of biological vs scrambled point-light displays), includes a healthy adult group (n=48, ages 20–35), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., biological>scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with tables/figures and cluster-correction details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI during an emotional sentence attribution task tied to social cognition (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, the paper does not present an unambiguous, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is explicitly and separately reported for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The reported results are a main effect of task (across groups), between-group contrasts (CON > PAT), and a task×group interaction identifying regions where controls > patients for EMO–GRAM; there is no clearly reported unmasked, within-controls whole-brain EMO>GRAM map or table of healthy-group coordinates identified as a standalone healthy-group task effect. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures described).

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based functional MRI while participants performed a social-affective judgment task (rating emotions evoked by images of social groups), directly addressing social perception/understanding of others. Participants were healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5), satisfying the sample-age criterion. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and contrast results (e.g., mPFC, insula, amygdala activations) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain effects (Talairach coordinates, t-values) and in-text contrasts, fulfilling the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) targeting social interaction and responses to unreciprocated cooperation, satisfying I3. Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22 (N≈304), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain results (e.g., main effect CD>CC in whole-brain analyses, referenced figures and supplemental whole-brain figures/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study that uses social-related tasks (empathic and forgivability judgements), satisfying the review topic. The sample comprises ten volunteers described as study participants (healthy adults), meeting the sample requirement for a healthy adult group. The abstract reports group-level brain activations (e.g., left superior frontal gyrus, orbitofrontal gyrus, precuneus, etc.), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results are reported for the healthy group. Results are described in text/tables (activation loci), so whole-brain evidence is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task study of social/empathy processing (viewing human and animal suffering), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=60; ages 18–60) with within-group and between-group task contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample/paired t-tests, ANOVA interaction), corrected results (FWE) and cluster coordinates, as well as conjunction and masking procedures; results are presented with MNI coordinates and statistical thresholds. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion E4: The study includes fMRI social tasks and a healthy control group aged 50–60 (I3 and I4 are satisfied). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain maps are for the combined sample (whole group) and ROI/small-volume corrected analyses and between-group contrasts (Cocaine > Control). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task effect reported) and meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete.
