This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (10 right-handed adults, mean age 26.9), and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs other, other vs self) with cluster-corrected thresholding and tables of MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (facial emotion recognition) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and familywise-error–corrected statistics (e.g., amygdala clusters, whole-brain regression results). Sample consists of healthy adult males (n=116, mean age 24.7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social attribution (a social-related task) that includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–65) reported separately. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group-by-empathy interaction and related group-specific effects) with cluster-level family-wise error correction and names specific brain regions showing effects in controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult group data reported).

This fMRI study used an explicit facial emotion identification task (social perception of others' emotions), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=22; mean age 31.7 years), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain ‘faces minus animals’ activation maps for the HC group (one-sample t tests and FDR-corrected results; figures and tables of activation foci are provided), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (satisfying acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: The study employed task-based fMRI during a social decision-making (modified prisoner’s dilemma) task (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 23–45) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy group (e.g., HC (COMP > CONT), HC (COOP > CONT), conjunctions and within-group Task > Control results) with tables/coordinates and cluster-level correction (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports fMRI task activations during a social-related task (imaginary sentence completion about mother/father) involving attachment/affiliation and social cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; mean age ~28) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results for the control group (one-sample t tests; results presented in Table 2 and described in the text). Whole-brain maps/coordinates for the healthy group are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within adult age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This empirical fMRI study investigates gesture planning and execution, a form of social communication, using task-based fMRI in a sample that includes a healthy adult control group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group (healthy controls) results (within-group results noted in Analyses S2/S3 and whole-brain second-level analyses described with thresholds and clusters). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants with separate healthy-group reporting), I5 (whole-brain group-level healthy-control task maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines moral (social) processing and uses task-based fMRI (meets I3). However, the sample comprises only incarcerated participants divided into high- and low-psychopathy groups; there is no separate healthy adult (non-clinical/non-forensic) control group or a reported healthy-group whole-brain task effect (therefore I4 and I5 are not met). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group and parametric contrasts but only within the forensic sample; accordingly it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/subgroup contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study uses fMRI during a social perception task (dataset from a social perception paradigm) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the primary reported results are seed-based intrinsic/background functional connectivity analyses and between-group connectivity contrasts; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (no unmasked whole-brain task activation map for HC is reported in the main text). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based/connectivity/resting-type analyses without also reporting a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (observation of risk-taking vs safe actions) that probes social cognition/emotional processing. Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18.1–22.8 (within 18–65) with screening for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (risk-taking vs safe) analyzed with SPM and presents peak coordinates and cluster results (MNI/Talairach), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social/emotion-related task (facial affect matching) during fMRI, satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult comparison group (n=12, ages within 18–65), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the healthy group (within-group Emotion Match > Shape Match contrasts, tables of coordinates and figures), satisfying I5 and the reporting format requirement I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-person perception task (likeability ratings of animated faces) that manipulates gaze direction and duration—clearly a social-related process. The sample includes a healthy control group of adults (n=13; ages 24–36) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (e.g., CON_DG > CON_AG, parametric modulation of gaze duration) with cluster- and voxel-level statistics and reported coordinates. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-out-of-range, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI to probe social-related processing (perception of others’ pupils/coherence between observer and observed), (I4) Healthy adult sample reported (N=14, mean age 22, 18–65 range), (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (main effects and interactions reported with whole-brain thresholds and coordinate tables), (I6) Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion provided. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (Cyberball social rejection), fulfilling I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=16 adults, female), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps (e.g., exclusion>inclusion main effects surviving cluster-level FWE correction) and provides peak coordinates and tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Results are not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses, and healthy participants are clearly reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (Cyberball) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps for healthy controls (within-group analysis showing mPFC/vACC activation with increasing exclusion). The paper includes a healthy adult control group reported separately from the schizophrenia group. Whole-brain results are reported with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinates. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study examines social cognitive processing (belief and emotion attribution) using task-based fMRI (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately from the schizophrenia group (controls N=14) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and descriptions for the healthy/control group (within-group activations and coordinates are described for both tasks) (I5,I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and participants are adult controls).

This study used fMRI during a social cognition task (HCP Animated Triangles) and reports task-related BOLD activation for healthy control participants separately. Healthy controls (n=25) are analyzed and results for the control group are presented with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (MNI coordinates, T-values) thresholded at p<0.05 FWE whole-brain corrected and shown in figures/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps for controls), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social exclusion, punishment/forgiveness) using Cyberball and a modified Dictator Game (I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, mean age 20.7) with exclusions applied appropriately (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with peak coordinates, tables, and figures from the healthy participant group (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages are within 18–65, and this is an empirical study with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=34, ages 18–39) that directly manipulates forms of psychological distance including an objective/social distancing condition (instructing participants to view images as an objective observer). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise contrasts and cluster tables/figures (mass univariate contrasts, conjunction analysis, and multivariate classification) clearly from the healthy sample. Results are reported in tables of coordinates and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task via social/objective distancing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing: judgments of pride (a self-conscious/social emotion) and joy. Participants: 16 healthy adult (mean age 21.3–21.5) university students (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (joy minus neutral; pride minus neutral; pride minus joy) with SPM, thresholding, tables of peak coordinates, and figures—meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly and separately. The full article text including methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates perception/understanding of others’ emotional facial expressions (social-related processing). Participants: 27 healthy adults (mean age 27) — meets age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste) analyzed with random-effects SPM2 and reports cluster coordinates, tables and figures. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (an ROI SVC was used but whole-brain results are reported). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception/understanding of infant emotional faces) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps and between-group contrasts. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (new mothers and nulliparous women) aged well within 18–65, with results for the healthy groups reported separately. Whole-brain analyses were performed using SPM12 with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction; contrasts (happy vs neutral, sad vs neutral, etc.) and group effects are described in the main text (tables/coordinates referenced). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (N=34, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (SIT vs NEUT) with family-wise-error (FWE) whole-brain correction and provides coordinates and ROI-corrected results; parametric and connectivity analyses are also detailed. Results for the healthy/control group are reported explicitly (between-group design but healthy-group effects and within-group contrasts are presented). Thus the study meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study using the Cyberball social exclusion task (a social-related paradigm) with a healthy control group reported separately. Whole-brain, voxelwise within-group results are reported for healthy controls (main effect of condition in left anterior insula; voxelwise FWE-corrected p-values and coordinates provided). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group), I5 (group-level whole-brain healthy-group task effect), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 25) using a Face Matching Task assessing perception of others’ emotions (social-related processing). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests for contrasts: neutral+fear > control; fear > neutral; fear > neutral+control) reported at second level (results referenced in main text and Supplementary Material), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for healthy group), and I6 (maps/results described and available in supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

This paper reports task-based fMRI data including multiple social-cognition tasks (false-belief ToM, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes-intention, face trustworthiness, vocalizations), i.e. social-related processing. The sample comprises 78 healthy adults (age range 18–40), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (voxelwise p<0.05 FWE-corrected), figures, and a supplementary table of peak coordinates; maps are also available via NeuroVault/HBP links. These meet the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (self- and other-reflection; perceptions of self and close other), includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (21 HCs), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy controls (contrasts self>semantic and other>semantic) with voxelwise/FWE-corrected results and figures/tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity trait judgments) in healthy adult participants (n=37, mean age 22.9), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with voxelwise statistics (FDR-corrected) and tables of activations. Whole-brain regression and gPPI results are reported and clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies the review’s fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (Ultimatum Game with subsequent social memory task), using healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 19.9, screened for neuropsychiatric disorders). The authors present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3-level mixed effects GLM), corrected for multiple comparisons (cluster correction Z>2.3, p<0.05), and report loci and tables of regions/coordinates associated with expectation violation contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, imaging details, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (distancing vs. looking at negative and neutral interpersonal images) (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16; mean age 31.8) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2 GLM, conjunction and contrast analyses, corrected thresholds) and describes healthy-group task effects and contrasts, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/tables (or supplementary material is reported), consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or age-only sample, and this is an empirical fMRI study). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (emotion recognition of one’s own vs. unknown child), includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without ELM) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics). Specifically, whole-brain within-group effects are reported (e.g., CON mothers show a familiarity effect in the medial frontal gyrus) and whole-brain across-group and per-group contrasts (happy>neutral, own>unknown) are presented. Reporting includes voxelwise, whole-brain results (tables/coordinates and text). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

While the study uses task-based fMRI of a social interaction (multi-round trust game) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met), it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain within-group (healthy/control) task activation map. The only whole-brain voxelwise results presented are exploratory between-group contrasts (control > patients) rather than an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing to meet I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses without any task-evoked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (participants are children/adolescents, age range 6.5–18.7, with no healthy adult subgroup aged 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI study of social-related processing — it uses resting-state fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65; sample consists of male children/adolescents and clinical ASD group), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy adult group). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during a Theory-of-Mind paradigm (social cognition/self- and other-understanding), tested in healthy adult participants (undergraduate groups, mean ages ~19.7–21.6, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (within-group effects for the low-PP healthy group and whole-brain contrasts with peak coordinates and figures; FWE/FDR-corrected results are described). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state only, and within-group healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition (voice-face) in healthy adults (N=16), so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are met. However, the paper reports results focused on ROI-corrected voxelwise analyses and PPI connectivity; the authors state there were no significant results at P<0.05 FWE for the whole brain without the covariate, and all reported activations are reported with ROI-based FWE correction or limited to predefined ROIs. The review requires at least one group-level whole-brain (unmasked/whole-brain) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5), which is not provided. Therefore this study meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E2. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (exp. 3) in healthy adult participants (N=21) using a task that involves retrieval of real-life, socially relevant events (oral examination interactions) tied to self/other and bodily-self processing, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activations (baseline contrasts and interaction effects) with coordinates and corrected statistics (including hippocampal small-volume correction) and describes these results for the healthy/control group separately. Participants are healthy adults (students) within the target age range. The study is empirical and not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines neural activity during a joint-action leading/following task (a social-interaction paradigm engaging perception/understanding of others and social coordination). Participants are healthy adults (mean ages ~40), n=18, meeting age/sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, conjunction [Leading>Rest] ∩ [Following>Rest]) with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates; results are presented for the whole healthy group and subgroups. Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group activation maps relevant to social processing. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of face perception that explicitly manipulates changeable, social aspects of faces (gaze direction, emotional expression, head/viewpoint) — constructs directly relevant to Social Communication (I3). The sample comprises eight healthy adult observers (healthy adult group reported; I4). The paper reports group-level statistical maps/analyses (FEAT Z-statistic images, Talairach coordinates, group-averaged time courses and reported coordinates/figures), meeting the whole-brain, voxelwise reporting requirement (I5) and presents coordinates/figures consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes a healthy adult task activation map, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence is slightly reduced because exact participant ages (18–65) are not explicitly stated, but participants are described as typical healthy adult observers and ethical approval/consent was obtained, so inclusion is appropriate.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind) using task-based contrasts (Person-Description and False-Belief). It reports results for a healthy adult control group (non-FHR) separately, including within-group, whole-brain one-sample t-tests and tables of peak coordinates (Table 3) and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing using a pseudo-interactive joke task (action-outcome contingency), directly probing self/other social processing and reward. Sample: 38 healthy adult participants (ages 19–29) with analyses reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER; action-outcome interaction) with cluster-level FWE correction, tables of coordinates, and figures—meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is a task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion recognition (socially relevant stimuli: angry, fearful, etc.) in healthy adult males (age 21–33). The paper reports group-level whole-brain (whole-slab) analyses with activation maps and voxelwise results (thresholds reported, figures shown) and provides coordinate-based results for several regions, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus criteria for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group results are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using dyadic (dfMRI) scanning during a social task (face-to-face eye contact), meeting the review’s social-processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults (19 pairs; ages 18–33) reported separately, satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (group GLM for tasks A and B; paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous systems), with cluster results, MNI coordinates, atlas labels, and thresholding described (Table 3, Figs 3–5). Thus whole-brain healthy-group results are available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (naturalistic approval/disapproval videos) in healthy adults (N=37; mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with familywise-error corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates and maps. Although ROI analyses are also reported, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for the healthy sample are clearly described. Thus all required inclusion criteria for fMRI social-processing studies in healthy adults are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (implicit social stimulus processing) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 28 healthy right-handed adults aged 30–50 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (ANOVA across the 28 subjects), conjunction and direct contrasts, thresholded and reported with cluster sizes and MNI coordinates, and figures/tables of results. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. Participants: 19 healthy, right-handed adults aged 19–28 (meets I4). Task: categorical knowledge and feature verification tasks included social-category (stereotype) judgments (meets I3). Analyses: whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts reported (e.g., ‘social’>‘non-social’ and ‘non-social’>‘social’) with tables of peak voxels and figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is original empirical fMRI data (not a review; E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion included). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment manipulating social context (collaboration, competition) during a handgrip effort task—i.e., a social-related task—and includes healthy adult participants (N=32, ages 18–39). The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results, cluster-level FWE correction) with tables/figures of activations (e.g., ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an fMRI study of empathy (a social-related process—perception/understanding of others) using task-based BOLD in healthy adults (N=32; mean age 19.9, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts, conjunction analyses, cluster thresholds and coordinates; tables/figures described) clearly identified as healthy group results. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within age range). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (1) fMRI during a social-related task (passive viewing of faces vs scenes; face perception—social processing); (2) healthy adult sample (final N=44 males, age 18–32); (3) reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (faces > scenes) with tables/coordinates and GLM results; (4) whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not ROI-only, not resting-state–only (task activation reported), includes within-range adults, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE.

This study used fMRI with a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task and included a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper primarily reports seed-based functional connectivity (seeded voxel correlations) and between-group connectivity differences (BPD vs. controls) for ToM and resting-state networks, and does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (either as a main effect or within-group contrast). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only seed-based/connectivity/resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. I3 and I4 met; I5 not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–34) that uses a passive action observation task probing action perception/understanding (mirror system) — a social-related construct. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts, thresholded and reported with coordinates and peaks) for the healthy control groups and describes results across mirror system areas. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-processing task requirement, the healthy adult sample requirement, and provides whole-brain group-level task activation maps clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under the social-related construct ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (I3). Participants are healthy adults (ages 19–24), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM), including reported coordinates and cluster-level statistics for contrasts (e.g., Morph 50% self vs. friend), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within range, and it is empirical).

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognitive task (neutral face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM), in a sample of healthy adult participants (N=74; genotyping subset N=73). Whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests, within-subject ANOVA) are reported with FWE-corrected results and figures; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are clearly described. Full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind) in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects ANOVAs), thresholded to whole-brain-corrected significance and summarized in Table 1 and figures (contrasts such as mentalising>factual and parametric modulation). Participants are healthy adults within 18–65 (Experiment 2 mean age 22; Experiment 1 range 18–60). Whole-brain results are clearly reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion requirements: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-emotional approach-avoidance task (I3), includes a large sample of healthy adults aged 18–43 with results reported for the healthy group (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain task analyses and contrasts (explicit whole-brain analyses and task effects are described and assessed at the whole-brain level) with results presented in text/figures/tables (I5,I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and core analyses are described, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical).

This fMRI study examines social-related processing (rapid fearful face perception) in adults and includes a healthy adult control group whose results are reported separately. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not limited to abstract), and the authors report whole-brain analyses (FLAME whole-brain analyses described in Appendix A and Supplementary Table 1) with significant clusters for the control group for the fearful face > scramble contrast. Thus inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (fMRI social task: emotional face processing), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the control group are reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/appendix and supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains healthy adults 18–65, empirical data). Full text appears complete.

The study uses task fMRI of emotion-word processing (a social-related construct: perception/understanding of self/others) and reports a healthy adult control group, but it does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. The results mostly report pooled (all participants) whole-brain maps, between-group (control > ASC) whole-brain contrasts, and ROI analyses; I cannot find a standalone, unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect (main effect or within-group contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map).

This paper reports task-based fMRI of gesture–speech integration, a social-communication task (I3). It includes healthy adult samples (H-group, C-group) reported separately with ages in the 19–32 range and matched controls (I4). The manuscript presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for the healthy/control groups (contrasts and conjunctions; coordinates and cluster tables referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study uses fMRI and discusses social-cognitive processes (e.g., mental state attribution) and includes healthy young adults (18–22). However, the paper’s whole-brain task activation results are reported for the full mixed-age sample (ages 10–22) or for age-related regressions; the authors do not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from a healthy adult (18–65) subgroup. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-adult whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI task involving social-related processes) and I4 (sample includes healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) directly apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social cognition (eye-gaze/intention processing), satisfying the social-related task requirement. It includes a neurologically normal healthy adult comparison group (n=9; mean age ~23.4, range within 18–65) with results reported separately. The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps and reports stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and figures for the healthy/control group (i.e., unmasked within-group task effects), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy group are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI probing social-emotional face processing (fearful and calm faces), includes a healthy adult control group (mean age 39.8, n=13), and reports group-level whole-brain within-group activation maps for the control group (robust bilateral amygdala activation reported with P<0.05 corrected). The task is clearly social-related (perception/understanding of others). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI task probing self-referential processing and perspective-taking (social-related constructs: perception/understanding of self and others), meeting the review’s scope. It includes a healthy control group with within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation contrasts clearly reported for the healthy/control group (e.g., self>other within HC; reported clusters/coordinates and figures/tables). Results for the healthy group are reported separately from the clinical UHR group. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (core article content present). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. Minor uncertainty about explicit ages of healthy participants (HC age range not verbatim), but demographics and recruitment imply adult controls; confidence set to 0.85.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI in a social context (adult expert advice) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy adult group. The reported whole-brain voxelwise analyses focus on developmental (between-group) contrasts and age-related effects, and subsequent within-age-group tests are reported as ROI/extracted-beta comparisons. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic investigator thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback) during task-based fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21, age range 21–39), meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses and corrected statistical maps/activation tables for the healthy group (negative social feedback > positive social feedback under placebo and drug conditions), with coordinates and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Exclusion rationale: E4 is met — the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (patient vs. control) and region-wise percent signal extractions; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (control) task activation map or clearly reported voxelwise healthy-group contrast maps in the main text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related attribution task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map for the healthy/control group is provided), and I6 (while coordinates/tables are reported, they reflect between-group contrasts and are not clearly described as an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

Although this prospective study used fMRI during a social interpersonal task (a modified Ultimatum Game) with healthy adult participants (soldiers and civilians), the full text reports ROI-based analyses (β extraction from vmPFC and brainstem/LC clusters identified previously) rather than presenting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group. Methods describe GLMs but the reported results and figures focus on ROI activations and ROI-change correlations. Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain task activation evidence (I5 not satisfied) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map). Full text appears complete.

fMRI task involves social-related processing (perception of others’ facial emotions, including disgust linked to social rejection), includes a healthy adult control group (n=40) with results reported separately, and the paper reports exploratory whole-brain analyses presented in the supplementary material (i.e., group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results). Core article contains full methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that manipulates social evaluation (praise vs criticism of others vs objects), involving healthy adult participants (n=30, ages 20–25). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial ANOVA, FWE-corrected thresholds, peak MNI coordinates, figures and supplementary tables) clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for task-related fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain results and acceptable reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (dynamic facial-expression perception and imagery) in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age ~25), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM/RFX analyses and thresholded statistical maps (localizer and imagery runs, whole-brain comparisons across groups) rather than ROI-only results. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal response to infant cry; attachment/affiliation), conducted in adults (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1, within 18–65) who are described as not meeting current major depressive episode criteria at scanning. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (own cry > control/other cry) using FSL with cluster correction and presents coordinates, tables, and figures of activation clusters. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results clearly described with tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (incidental learning and memory of social networks) in healthy adults (N=22; ages 18–34). The task is social-related (learning and recalling relationships between faces) and involved task-evoked fMRI during face viewing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise RSA searchlight results (nonparametric one-sample t-test, FWE-corrected clusters with MNI coordinates and cluster sizes), which satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample) apply.

The study uses fMRI with an emotional face (social) go/no-go task and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the neurotypical control group (meets I3, I5, I6). However, the healthy/control sample includes participants aged 12–23 and is not restricted to adults 18–65; no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup is analyzed or reported. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) directly apply beyond the failure to meet I4.

Excluded because the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social processes: ToM and empathy) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group aged 18–65 reported separately). However it primarily reports between-group contrasts and conjunctions testing diagnosis effects and interactions, and does not present a clearly identified whole-brain group-level task effect for the healthy/control group (no unmasked controls-only main-effect or within-group whole-brain statistical map is reported). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore it must be excluded. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map not provided).

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related emotion-processing task relevant to social cognition) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group aged within 18–65). However, the full text does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain findings are either the main effect across all subjects and between-group contrasts (group differences), and ROI analyses; there is no clearly described unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 is met (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of emotional (affective) speech comprehension—a social cognitive task involving perception and understanding of others' emotions. It reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with voxelwise SPM analyses and corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults aged 18–53 (within 18–65). Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented (figures, tables, coordinates). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=38, ages 18–34) that uses a social-processing task (false-belief perspective-taking localizer) during fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain task results (e.g., False Belief > FACT contrasts, peak coordinates [52, -56, 18] and reported whole-brain analyses/supplement). Whole-brain ROI coordinates and contrasts are provided and the paper reports task-evoked activation maps and connectivity analyses. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported via coordinates/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of social decision-making (trust game) in healthy adult participants (initial N=31, final N=29 after exclusions). The task examines reputation-based trust (a social construct: perception and understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3DClustSim cluster-corrected thresholds) and provides coordinates and figures for whole-brain results (main effect of partner), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (modified ‘Reading the Mind in the Eyes’), includes a healthy adult control group (HC; n=12, ages 23–55) whose data are reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests for each of the four groups including HC, with thresholding and figures showing healthy-group activation maps and coordinates). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described (methods and Results, Fig.2 and coordinate-based reporting for contrasts). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is original empirical work). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates neural processing of others' actions (auditory mirror system) — a social-cognitive task (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26 behavioral; n=11 in fMRI; ages 21–29), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with statistical maps, cluster-level inference, and tables/figures of activations. Results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy/sympathy) using task-based stimuli, meeting the review’s focus. The sample includes healthy adult participants (age range 7–40, thus includes adults 18–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (PCS–NPS and PCO–PCS) and voxelwise correlation analyses, with results presented as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly described and thresholded. Therefore it satisfies the requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy participants and provides whole-brain evidence suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion met: E4. The paper reports task activation only as between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. (b) Inclusion met: I3 (uses fMRI with a social-related task — facial expression discrimination), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–65). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map clearly identified as from the healthy/control group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results reported in tables/figures/text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5 and meeting exclusion E4.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E4 — the study reports only patient-group effects (CET vs EST) and does not include or report an unmasked whole-brain task activation map from a healthy/control group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — the fMRI task (POP) is a cognitive control (non-social) paradigm, not a social-related task; I4 — no healthy adult participant group is included or reported separately; I5 — no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported for a healthy/control group. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study does not meet the review eligibility and should be excluded.

This fMRI study of social processing (watching a TV episode) includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain analyses, so it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The authors report (a) a whole-brain map collapsed across all subjects and (b) between-group contrasts (NT > ASD) and ROI-based analyses, but I find no unmasked, whole-brain NT (healthy-only) task activation map or contrast described as coming solely from the healthy group. Therefore I5 is not met. This triggers exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (empathy) using face stimuli—clearly a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (n=26, ages ~24), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SELF- and OTHER-task vs high-level baseline) analyzed with random-effects SPM and presents whole-brain thresholded maps and tables of peak coordinates. Results for the healthy control group are reported separately and meet reporting standards (tables/figures and text). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (male college students, ages within 18–65) that uses a social/affiliation paradigm (rival-fan memory retrieval, perspective-taking, self-referential and social-cognition processes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM random-effects, parametric and categorical contrasts, tables of activations, and small-volume corrections), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind task) in healthy adult participants (n=109). The Methods and Results report a group-level whole-brain task contrast (ToM > control) across all healthy subjects, thresholded and presented in figures/tables (P<0.01 FWE for main effect; voxelwise genotype effects also reported FDR-corrected). The task probes social-related processing (mentalising), sample comprises healthy adults, and whole-brain group-level activation maps/effects for the healthy group are clearly reported in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of emotion regulation using participant-generated autobiographical social situations and negative self-beliefs—i.e., social-related processing focused on perception/understanding of self in social contexts. Sample: 35 healthy adults aged 22.6–55.4, meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects group maps), tables of activations, figures, and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly identified as from the healthy/control group. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ actions; mentalizing vs mirror systems) using a task where participants classify biological vs artificial motion, satisfying the review’s social-processing scope. Sample: healthy adult participants reported (n=12, right-handed, mean age 27.3±4.7), meeting the age and healthy-group requirement. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses are reported using SPM2 with FDR correction and tables of activated regions/coordinates (Tables 1 and 2) and figures; thus whole-brain evidence is available and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult, or non-empirical paper). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with tables of significant regions, corrected thresholds, and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Behavioral and imaging methods, participant characteristics, and univariate and multivariate analyses are fully described for the healthy sample. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult perceivers (n=16, mean age 19.1) that examines neural responses during social tasks (emotion and eye-gaze rating). The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (parametric modulators, contrasts, conjunctions) with reported coordinates, figures, and tables, clearly coming from the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (use of fMRI in social-related tasks; healthy adult sample; whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported; coordinate and figure reporting acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social perceptual decision task manipulating social context (partners) to study private-public mappings; the task and analyses are social-related (social communication/context). The sample comprises 28 healthy adults (mean age 26.36), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (e.g., whole-brain activations for quadratic context, cluster-level FWE-corrected results) and provides group statistical maps on NeuroVault. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (learning about and simulating others’ inter-temporal preferences and social influence on valuation) using a task that requires evaluating self and others. The sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (behavioral N=27, fMRI N=29 with exclusions), with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (second-level random effects analyses, cluster-defining thresholds, FWE-corrected clusters) with coordinates and statistical maps described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI with a social vs non-social incentive delay paradigm and includes a healthy adult control group, but the paper reports results primarily as between-group contrasts and interactions (BPD vs HC) and ROI analyses. The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone (e.g., HC social>non-social whole-brain contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Ultimatum Game (a social decision-making task) and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts. The sample includes a healthy adult group (young adults age 19–28) with results for that group reported separately. The paper provides voxelwise contrasts (unfair–fair) and group-level statistical maps/tables for the adult group. Reporting of whole-brain results is in figures/tables and described in text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adult participants (N=32, females, mean age 22.7). The tasks are social-cognitive (mentalizing, empathy for pain, prosocial decision), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar; Painful > Non-Painful) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of coordinates/results. Healthy adult sample and separate reporting of healthy-group results are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (satisfying I4, I5, I6). However, the experimental task is a sensorimotor synchronization dual-task (finger tapping to an auditory pacing signal with an n-back visual task) and was not designed or manipulated as a social task. Although the authors speculate that medial prefrontal activations may reflect mentalizing or perspective-taking, the paradigm does not involve explicit social interaction, social stimuli, or instructions to process others’ minds/intentions; therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) performing a social-related task (perception/integration of others’ emotional facial and vocal cues), satisfying the review’s domain (social perception/understanding of others). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provide tables of coordinates and whole-brain thresholds (explicit whole-brain contrasts and conjunctions are described), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical).

The full text reports an fMRI study using a social task (threshold public goods game) with model-based analyses. Sample: 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.5), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (FWE-corrected cluster-level results) and provides unthresholded maps on NeuroVault. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, and whole-brain results for the healthy sample are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence) in healthy adult participants (mean age 20.4, n=12 analyzed). The task is explicitly social and uses task-evoked BOLD responses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected significance thresholds (i.e., whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines neural and behavioral responses to social touch (manual foot massage) versus machine-administered touch in healthy adult participants. The sample consists of healthy adults (46 males, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-sample and paired t-tests; whole-brain FDR-corrected results and statistical maps are described and displayed), and combined real and imagined massage contrasts are clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Thus it satisfies the review’s fMRI social-processing objective and meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical study issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the fMRI analyses were conducted within an a priori bilateral amygdala ROI (small-volume/cluster correction within the amygdala) and the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—automatic processing of facial emotion) and I4 (healthy adult control group, N=35, reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level healthy-control task activation map reported). Exclusion criteria triggered: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (results primarily reported as group comparisons/interactions without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants imagined encountering neutral faces embedded in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant everyday social situations (social communication / perception of others). Sample: healthy adult participants (17 analyzed; ages 20–36) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects ANOVAs; cluster-corrected thresholds; tables/coordinates and figures provided), not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. I recommend inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self-, mother- and celebrity-judgments) probing self- and other-processing. The sample consists of healthy adult Chinese college students (final N=34; right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self- vs celebrity, mother- vs celebrity) and regression/moderation analyses with tables of coordinates (Tables 2 and 3) and figures, with correction/threshold details—satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-outside-range, or non-empirical paper issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment examining neural correlates of receiving empathic vs. unempathic social comments (social-related processing). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=20, mean age 26) with no neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., empathic>unempathic, negative>positive feedback) with cluster thresholds and FWE-corrected results and tables of activations. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures meets acceptable reporting standards. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, etc.) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study uses resting-state fMRI seed-based functional connectivity to relate amygdala subregion connectivity to long-term stigma change in a healthy adult sample. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes healthy adults aged 18–65, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task; fMRI was resting-state), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion. Therefore the paper does not meet the requirement for task-evoked whole-brain fMRI evidence and must be excluded.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports group × drug interactions and provides brain maps collapsed across group/drug, but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related emotional face matching task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 21–64, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map presented) and I6 (no healthy-group whole-brain results clearly described for controls in text/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a socio-emotional preference task (Preference vs Gender) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 23–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Preference>Gender and other contrasts) thresholded at p<0.05 FDR-corrected and provides tables of activation peaks and figures with coordinates. Core article content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment manipulating social competition (a social-related task involving social comparison/mentalizing). Sample: healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35; N=20 after exclusion), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion.
