The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no-competition; working-memory parametric modulators), including cluster thresholds, Monte Carlo correction, peak coordinates, and figures/tables describing whole-brain results. Whole-brain results are explicitly described for the healthy/control group (not limited to a narrow subgroup). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (reciprocity in the Trust Game) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate; regressions; ROI analyses supplement) with MNI coordinates, thresholding procedures, and correction details. All required inclusion criteria are met: (I3) social-related task using fMRI; (I4) healthy adult sample (18–22) reported separately; (I5) whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported and described; (I6) whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This paper uses task-based fMRI (cyberball social exclusion), a prototypical social-processing task (affiliation/attachment/social pain). Sample is healthy adults (N=71 final; female, mean age ~21.7, within 18–65). The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster statistics (initial whole-brain threshold p<0.001, with FWE small-volume corrections) and present coordinates and figures in the text/results. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/coordinates for healthy participant groups. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a social-related task (perception/recognition of own vs. others' body parts — perception/understanding of self and others). Sample sizes and recruitment indicate healthy adults. The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts used to localize regions (e.g., body minus objects, objects minus body parts, with Talairach coordinates and voxel counts for EBA, V1/2, LOC) and provides coordinate-level whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Although many analyses use ROI-extracted time courses and ANOVAs, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and coordinates are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22 males, mean age 24.2) performing social-related tasks (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance judgements). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (second-level SPM), thresholded at p<0.05 FWE, with activation maps and tables of coordinates reported for the healthy participant group. Results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. Therefore it satisfies the review objective and all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social evaluation/impression formation (social cognition) using task fMRI in healthy adults. The study includes a young adult group (ages 20–29), which satisfies the requirement for a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range (I4). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and contrasts (social vs. non-social; social-meaningful vs. social-irrelevant), conjunction analyses, and corrected cluster thresholds with peak locations reported (satisfying I5 and I6). The task is explicitly social-related (forming impressions; I3). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain results are reported, and study includes an eligible age group). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses task-based fMRI of self-referential processing (social-related construct: perception/understanding of self) and includes a healthy young adult group (ages 18–35), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper reports only group-level interactions and between-group contrasts (Age × Stereotypicality, Age × Threat/Resiliency) comparing older and younger adults and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or within-group whole-brain contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing: participants performed meaning-relatedness judgments on social concepts (social vs. animal-function word pairs). The sample includes healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (categorical subtraction at whole-brain thresholds, conjunction analyses, and coordinates reported in tables/figures), and whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perspective-taking/other-perspective self-referential task) in healthy adult participants (mean age 18.6, N=33), meeting the review focus. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (OS-P contrast) with whole-brain correction and also reports results from ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described in the methods and results (left medial PFC, left caudate). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This full-text reports empirical fMRI studies of social-affective processing in healthy adult participants. The paper includes two group-level fMRI experiments (fMRI1, fMRI2) using a social/empathy visuo-tactile paradigm, with whole-brain random-effects analyses (fMRI1 reported whole-brain results; fMRI2 used independent localizer-based SVC but also performed whole-brain analyses and reports group-level task contrasts and coordinates). Samples consist of healthy adult participants (female undergraduates) reported separately for each experiment. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts for the healthy groups are reported (interaction contrasts, peak coordinates, and tables/figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (effortful control of interpersonal trust/distrust) in healthy adult participants (n=59–60, mean age ~20, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, and combined contrasts) with family-wise error correction and provides tables/figures and MNI coordinates. Whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported in the text/tables/figures, and ROI analyses are supplementary but do not replace whole-brain results. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of intention inference including an explicitly social task (Social Basic: cooperation vs. defection), addresses perception/understanding of others (social cognition), and manipulates priors and sensory evidence. Participants: 18 healthy adults aged 24–54 (within 18–65). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (GLM, voxelwise and clusterwise thresholds, group-level SPM, coordinates provided) and PPI/DCM connectivity analyses; results for the healthy sample are presented (not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study investigating processing of others' decisions (social cognition). It scanned 12 healthy adult participants (mean age 21) and reports group-level, voxelwise second-level SPM analyses (ANOVA contrasts and reported peak coordinates/figures), with small-volume correction applied to the ACC. Whole-brain voxelwise group results are described and coordinates/figures are provided for healthy subjects. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI experiment investigating social communication/perception of others (vitality forms) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. The sample includes healthy adults (n=15, mean age 23.3), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., gentle vs control; rude vs control), with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (p<0.05). Results include conjunctions and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self vs. other processing with romantic partner video vignettes) in healthy adults aged 23–40. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, ANOVA) with voxelwise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (deception/sophisticated deception in strategic interactions; involves theory-of-mind/social cognition). Sample: healthy adults (N=34, ages 21–32) with group-level analyses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (Bayesian second-level posterior probability maps) and tables of coordinates for multiple contrasts (Tables 3–8; figures shown), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task is social and performed during fMRI. No exclusion criteria are met: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and this is empirical original data. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI to study interpersonal (affective) touch, a clearly social-related paradigm (affiliation/ social communication). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=30 after one exclusion), mean age 40.5, screened for depression and autistic traits, falling within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (activation and deactivation maps), with FWE-corrected results and whole-brain analyses described in the text/tables/figures (including a “touch pleasantness weighted” whole-brain contrast). Whole-brain results are reported and anatomically defined; supplementary results and tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range samples) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=60; ages 18–60) that uses a social-related task (observation of mouth actions/oral communicative actions and biting across human and animal actors) probing social communication and empathy. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (second-level random effects SPM analyses, p<0.05 FWE), with tables/figures of activations and within-group contrasts for the healthy participant groups. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study reports task-evoked activation during an action imitation/observation paradigm, a social-related process (perception/understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (N=16) with results for the healthy group reported separately. The paper reports within-group whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., imitation > nonimitative action; animated > nonanimated observation) with peak coordinates and corrected statistical maps described, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI study of self/other social cognition (trait judgments), using healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and statistical parametric maps with tables of coordinates and figures (SPM analyses, whole-brain thresholds described). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level results (I5), and allowance for coordinate/figure reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This fMRI study examines face-based social/emotional processing (Thatcher Illusion) and explicitly probes social/mentalizing regions; it includes a neurotypical healthy adult control group (N=18, mean age 25.8) reported separately; and it presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and statistical maps for the healthy/control group (within-group NT activation maps and thresholds reported). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) fMRI social-related task, (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately, (I5) whole-brain group-level results for controls, and (I6) acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in figures/text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study probing social cognition (predicting individuals’ preferences from group membership), with healthy adult participants (mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (contrasts, thresholding, cluster-FWE correction) and presents coordinates/activation maps and beta estimates. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLM), results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception of others) in healthy adults (n=18, age range 19–36). The task is social-related (face recognition/false recognition) meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65 meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked analyses using Random Effects (RFX) and cluster correction and provides Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right precentral and cingulate gyri), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (implicit perception of emotional facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., a within-group main effect or contrast for controls). Reported healthy-control results appear only as between-group contrasts (controls > patients) rather than an independent healthy-group whole-brain map. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study reports an fMRI experiment investigating perception of emotional body expressions (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages within 18–65). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FDR correction and Monte-Carlo cluster correction) clearly identified as coming from the healthy control group; ROI analyses are also reported but do not replace the whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing full assessment. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 20), using social-related tasks (inferring others’ vegetable preferences and categorical age judgments) that probe perception and understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and preprocessing, and group-level, random-effects GLM analyses with whole-brain contrast maps reported (Talairach coordinates, voxel clusters, tables/figures). Results include voxelwise activations in mPFC and other regions with coordinates and cluster sizes. All required inclusion criteria are met: fMRI during social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported (I5), and whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (observation of human/robot agents interacting with objects) using a task during functional MRI in healthy adults (final N=23, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (main effects of agent form and belief, interactions) with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster/FWE correction and provides peak coordinates and tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants to investigate neural coding of voice identity—a form of social perceptual processing (Perception and Understanding of Others/Social Communication). It reports group-level, voxelwise fMRI results (e.g., vocal > nonvocal localizer and correlations with distance-to-mean across TVA voxels) and presents whole-brain/group-level statistical maps and coordinates. The participant sample is healthy adults, and whole-brain, group-level analyses are clearly described. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of emotional face processing (a social-related perception/understanding of others task) in healthy adult volunteers. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Sample: 30 healthy, right-handed volunteers selected for genotype, screened for psychiatric disorders, with group-level results reported separately for the healthy groups. Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (whole-brain comparisons at p < .001 uncorrected; Supplementary Table S3 referenced) and main effects across all subjects are presented, satisfying the requirement for an unmasked, group-level healthy control task activation map. Coordinate tables and figures with group-level statistics are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI task study explicitly investigating self-face recognition (a social-cognitive construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), using an event-related BOLD paradigm. Participants are healthy adults (12 right-handed males, mean age 19.36), meeting the 18–65 age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., unknown vs. scrambled, familiar vs. unknown, self vs. familiar) analyzed in SPM with thresholding and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical data present).

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants learned moral status (cooperator/defector) via interactive Prisoner’s Dilemma and were scanned while making gender judgments of those faces — a clear social-related task. The sample consists of healthy adults (scanned n=11, ages 21–36). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and tables/figures of activations. Results are not limited to ROI, connectivity, or between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for task, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (affective and cognitive Theory of Mind), satisfying the social-task requirement. The sample is 23 healthy participants recruited from the general population (healthy adult group reported separately), meeting the sample criterion for a healthy adult group. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain FDR-corrected cluster results, tables/figures described), providing the required healthy-group whole-brain evidence. Results for AToM and CToM are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Note: exact participant ages are not explicitly listed in the provided text, but participants are described as healthy adults and age was used as a covariate; this introduces minor uncertainty reflected in the confidence score.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of a social task (Trust Game) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, but the reported second-level results are comparisons between two healthy subgroups (high-Mach vs low-Mach). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group as a whole (or for an unrestricted healthy group), only between-group contrasts. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 19–30), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain task-evoked map from a non-narrow healthy/control group). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in which healthy adult participants (n=36) performed an Other task requiring prediction of another person’s decisions—clearly a social-related task (simulation/theory-of-mind). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (significant clusters reported with corrected p-values and Talairach coordinates; Tables and figures show whole-brain results) based on the healthy participant group. Results for the healthy/control group are presented (behavioral and fMRI within-group effects). Reporting includes coordinate tables and figures consistent with whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social-processing studies in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Frith–Happé animation ToM task) in adults and reports results for a neurotypical healthy control group. The healthy control group (n=23) is within the 18–65 age range (19–56 reported) and is analyzed/reported separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain one-sample t-tests and whole-brain analyses for the NT/control group (results and supplementary whole-brain results are described and displayed), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social communicative/collaborative memory task (directors and matchers), investigating social cognition (mentalizing/theory of mind) and communication. The sample is healthy adults aged 18–33 and group results are reported for the healthy participants. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Collaborative > Individual, Individual > Arbitrary, Arbitrary > Individual) with cluster-corrected maps and tables of results; whole-brain ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain effects are primary. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis’ requirements for fMRI of social processing in healthy adults with whole-brain task activation maps.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study of social-related tasks in healthy adults and reports voxelwise activation and peak coordinates, the group-level statistical analyses reported in the paper were restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than presented as unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map from the healthy/control group) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (coordinates/tables/figures reporting results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (Ultimatum Game) involving healthy adult participants (controls and experienced meditators). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (within-group contrasts and between-group contrasts), provides voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables (MNI), and describes random-effects, cluster- and FDR-corrected results for the healthy groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E2 met: the paper reports fMRI task results using a priori ROI analyses (mPFC and amygdala masks) and presents ROI-restricted group contrasts; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: facial emotion identification — perception/understanding of others) and I4 (healthy adult group aged 20–31 reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked statistical map provided). I6 (not applicable because it requires whole-brain results in tables/figures). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it reports only ROI-restricted task analyses without whole-brain healthy-group activation maps (E2).

I3, I5, and I6 are satisfied: the study used fMRI during a social Theory-of-Mind task (RMET) in healthy participants and reports a group-level whole-brain ‘mind minus age’ contrast with voxelwise results (figures and thresholds). However, it fails I4: the healthy participant group age range is 51–84 (M=68.4), so the study does not provide a healthy adult sample restricted to 18–65 or a separate subgroup in that range. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E4, E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult age 18–65).

This fMRI study investigates perception/recognition of visual feedback as self vs other (visuo-motor and visuo-proprioceptive synchrony), which maps to ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (a social-related construct). Participants were healthy adults (16, median age 24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps) analyzed with SPM2 and provides tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination (a social-cognitive task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (emotional conditions versus baseline and versus neutral) analyzed for both groups, with voxelwise results, coordinate tables/figures, and FWE/uncorrected thresholds. Within-group contrasts for controls are described and illustrated (e.g., sad > neutral in controls shown in Fig. 3), satisfying the requirement for an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The manuscript reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of social processing (eye-gaze perception), using healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–30). Whole-brain, group-level second‑level voxelwise analyses are reported (variable vs. constant gaze contrasts and AQ regressions), with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates provided in the text and supplementary ROI checks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results reported), and I6 (coordinates and text description). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The full article text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (heterosexual and homosexual men and women, ages within 18–65) that used a task involving passive viewing of sexual stimuli (male and female genitals) to probe perception of others, reward and motor systems (including mirror-related PMv responses), which falls under social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, affiliation/sexual motivation). The paper reports group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain results with reported clusters/coordinates (and indicates whole-brain correction for non-ROI areas), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are in age range, and it is empirical). Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (action observation/representation of others’ actions and interactions), conducted in healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral, Squeeze > No Squeeze, 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with FWE correction and includes tables/figures of peak coordinates and statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (emotion recognition with morphed faces; a social JTC paradigm), with 47 healthy adult participants (age range 18–33). The paper presents group-level whole-brain task activation results (whole-brain analyses reported with FWE correction and a Table 1 of whole-brain results; ROI results also provided), and describes these results in text, figures, and tables. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study uses task-based fMRI of gaze processing (a social-related task) and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the typically developing (healthy/control) group (Table 2; coordinates), satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, the healthy/control group includes adolescents as well as adults (ages 16.1–42.4) and results are reported for the mixed-age TD group rather than for a healthy adult (18–65) subgroup specifically; therefore I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I4 missing), the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI using IAPS emotional picture viewing (including many images containing human faces) which indexes perception/evaluation of others’ emotional states—aligned with social-related constructs (Perception and Understanding of Others). It includes a separate healthy adult control group (NC) with results presented separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotion vs. neutral) and cluster-corrected statistical maps are reported for groups and subgroups (figures/tables and text), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and data/code availability are present. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4, n=16 after exclusions) investigating visual perspective taking — a social-cognitive process (perception/understanding of others). The task is social in nature (self vs. other perspective judgments). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; Consistent Self > Consistent Other) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of results and coordinates. Whole-brain analyses are explicitly described and attributed to the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain activation maps/coordinates.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~23) that uses task-based fMRI during social tasks (Cyberball and an iterated trust game). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain ANOVAs, parametric PE regressors) with coordinates, cluster correction, and figures/tables describing results for the healthy participant group. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of supramodal emotional (social) processing in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–34). The task is social-related (perception/integration of facial and vocal emotions). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, conjunctions, FDR-corrected maps; tables/figures with coordinates reported). All inclusion criteria for the review are met, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates processing of narratives with moral/protected values — a social-related task (social cognition, moral evaluation, understanding others). Participants are healthy adults (three groups; mean ages ~24–26; n=78 after exclusions), within the 18–65 range and reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., reading stories vs rest, protected-value vs nonprotected stories) with cluster correction; whole-brain results are described in the text and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of verbal irony implicating Theory of Mind and social communication (social cognition). Sample: twenty healthy adult participants (mean age 22) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Ironic > Literal) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction and provides coordinates and ROI analyses. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled fMRI study in 55 healthy adult males (mean age ~24.9) that used an explicit social-related task (extended Hariri face/scene matching including erotic/attachment and fearful social scenes), satisfying the social-processing construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (whole-brain FWE-corrected maps and contrasts are described and shown in figures/tables, with ROI analyses supplementary), clearly coming from the healthy participant group. Reporting includes whole-brain results in the main text and figures (and supplementary material), meeting the acceptable reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation and observation of communicative gestures) in healthy adults (20 analyzed; mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and cluster-corrected results with coordinate tables and figures (e.g., IMI>CT conjunction, S>NS contrasts, interaction analyses). Healthy-control results are reported separately and meet voxelwise whole-brain reporting standards. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, non-adult-only samples, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (comprehension of others' emotions) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–32). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., How>Why, Why>How) with tables of coordinates and SPM analyses, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activations).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during a social evaluation task (observation/evaluation of social encounters, perception/understanding of others); (I4) sample comprises healthy adult participants ages 18–29 (reported separately); (I5/I6) group-level voxelwise task contrasts and ANOVAs are reported with coordinates, figures, and cluster-level inference (second-level flexible factorial analyses and whole-brain/ROI-corrected statistical maps are described and tabulated). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, seed-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study (Study 2) that investigates social-cognitive processing (mentalizing/attribution of agency—perception and understanding of others) using a task of passive viewing of sexualized and clothed human targets. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (21 heterosexual men, age range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001 with cluster correction via AlphaSim) and presents whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3, Figures 2–4) identifying activations and correlations with hostile sexism. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (masked fearful/happy eye whites) with a social-related task (eye-region emotion processing) in healthy adult participants (initial N=50, analyzed N=43; mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level SPM random-effects analyses and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported whole-brain activations (pulvinar, ACC, orbitofrontal cortex) and supplementary tables, and also reports within-group/placebo effects. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, resting-state, or connectivity-only, and healthy adult group results are reported separately. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although the study uses task fMRI of self-referential (social-cognitive) processing and includes a healthy control group, it does not report a group-level whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper focuses on ROI- and seed-based voxelwise functional connectivity/network reconstructions and between-group connectivity differences (aMCI vs controls). This makes it a seed-based connectivity/task-network connectivity study without an unmasked, healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, thus violating the review requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only seed/functional connectivity results without healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge). The methods report an fMRI task manipulating social agent (bodies vs names) and social knowledge (trait vs neutral), with 21 healthy adult participants (age mean 24.6). Group-level whole-brain univariate results and connectivity (PPI) results are reported (Tables and figures described; voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction reported), and coordinates are provided. Thus the paper meets the review’s requirements for (i) task-based fMRI in social cognition, (ii) healthy adult sample, and (iii) reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (reported in text/tables/figures). The supplied full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain maps, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (self- and other-reflection). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=33, ages within 18–65) with results for the healthy group reported separately (within-group contrasts: Self>Facts, Other>Facts, Other>Self). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, cluster-level corrected (reported z thresholds, MNI coordinates, cluster sizes, Supplementary tables and figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of healthy-group whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (processing of dynamic vs static facial expressions), involving healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25) and reporting group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables (e.g., dynamic > static; ALE meta-analysis uses reported coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (prediction of others' behavior framed as desires vs. rules) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–44). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level flexible factorial models, cluster- and voxel-level correction, tables/coordinates and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- and other-referential recollection), using task-based fMRI and addressing social cognition constructs. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–29), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects), with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3; whole-brain and ROI/SVC reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 23–40) using a social-related task (viewing partner video-vignettes with self vs. other focus). The paper reports group-level analyses (e.g., the contrast self vs. other identifying the RTPJ as significant) and provides peak coordinates used for ROI selection, indicating whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map/contrast reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception and understanding of others via voices; identity and emotion recognition), meeting I3. Sample includes healthy adult participants (15 sighted, 7 congenitally/early blind; ages within adult range), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (univariate whole-brain GLM results, searchlight MVPA group-level maps, tables and figures of voxelwise results) satisfying I5 and I6. Full article includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and contains whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps for inclusion in the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=45, ages 18–34) using a reappraisal generation task (RGT) that requires participants to imagine anger-eliciting, interpersonal scenarios and generate reappraisals — a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of others, empathy/theory-of-mind processes. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and task contrasts) with FWE correction and reports activation clusters in standard tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task results), and I6 (results reported as tables/figures in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (Trust Game), a social-related task assessing perceptions/behavior toward others. Sample comprises healthy adult university students (final N=38, mean age ~23), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Fair – Control; Unfair – Control) and group comparisons, with tables of coordinates, figures, voxelwise thresholds and FWE correction—i.e., whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps are clearly reported. Results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports an fMRI investigation using the social cyberball task (a social-related paradigm) and includes a healthy adult control group (HC; N=17, ages 18–40). Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses for the healthy group are reported (main effect of condition in HC with FWE-corrected cluster results and region listings), satisfying the requirement for an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only-without-healthy-map, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Exclusion E4: No healthy adult control group whole-brain task map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—PANSIT-MC with mother–child affect clips) and I6 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult participant group reported separately — sample consists solely of depressed mothers of psychiatrically ill children), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map reported for a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included because it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain activation maps required by the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental simulation of personally familiar people), with healthy adult participants (n=23 after exclusions; age 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and feature-selected RSA analyses, including random-effects t tests, cluster-corrected statistical maps, peak coordinates and figures/tables of whole-brain results. Results are clearly reported for the healthy control sample. Thus it meets the fMRI social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult (18–65) participant group and the task is a non-social visual attention task. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (participants are children/adolescents; no healthy adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the fMRI task is non-social visual attention, not a social-related task) and I4 (no healthy adult sample; all participant groups are boys/children/adolescents). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=24, ages 19–31) performing a familiarity judgment for personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces—an explicitly social-related task involving perception/understanding of others and social cognition. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted using SPM5 with cluster-level correction and are reported in tables/figures (activation maps and peak coordinates). Post-scan behavioral measures and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P1–F1, repetition suppression contrasts) are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This is an fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure when observing human and robot agents) using task-based functional MRI (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–27 with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (repetition suppression and discrete event-related contrasts), with cluster-corrected results and whole-brain maps referenced and deposited on NeuroVault (meets I5 and I6). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=195, age 19–38) using a social interactive task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes mentalizing/social cognition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (ment > cont) analyzed with SPM8 and voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results (including coordinates and ROI follow-ups) are presented for the healthy sample. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of face individuation, which constitutes social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=15; mean age 24.8), satisfying the age and participant criteria. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (see 'Individuation task' whole-brain analysis, Supplementary Table S1 and Figure S1) reporting coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy control group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group-only; participants are within age range; empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and whole-brain supplementary results). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates implicit processing of facial emotions (fear vs neutral), which is a social-related task (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24) matched to patients and within the adult age range (I4). The paper reports group-level control results used to localize the amygdala seed (peak MNI coordinate −26,0,−20) derived from a control-group voxelwise analysis and describes control-group activation in text/coordinates; this satisfies the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5). Reporting of the control-group peak coordinate and description of the group-level activation meets the allowance for coordinate/figure-based reporting (I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: although the main analysis is PPI connectivity, a healthy-group task activation is reported, so E3/E4 do not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED for the review.

This fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group (N=13, ages >18) and uses a social-related task (perception of fearful faces). The paper reports group-level, within-control-group task contrasts and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (main effect of faces for controls) with coordinates and tables, satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps; results are reported both in text and tables/figures. Though small-volume correction was applied to a priori ROIs, the analyses began with a whole-brain threshold and the control-group activations (including amygdala, IOG, MPFC) are clearly identified. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes; mental-state and age-judgement versions) (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n≈25; ages 18–59) reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results for healthy controls (see Supplementary Tables S2 and S3) with cluster-wise FWE correction and voxelwise thresholds, i.e., unmasked whole-brain statistical maps/analyses (I5). Results are presented in main text, tables and figures (I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no resting/connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are provided, and participants are within age range).

This is an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (a social cognition/task involving perception and understanding of others). Sample: 50 healthy adults (mean age 20.1) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and whole-brain regression analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics (e.g., bilateral TPJ, medial PFC) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Behavioral and mediation analyses are reported, and whole-brain results are given in the main text/supplement. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social-processing task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task) contrasting mental-state vs age judgments (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=28) and age-matched control subgroups (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and corrected group Z statistic images from factorial models, and describes within-group/control-group effects (e.g., left MFG greater activity in controls; younger vs older control comparisons; Supporting Information, Table III), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (aged 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing and decision-making after provocation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (high>low provocation; decision and feedback phases) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction, clearly from the healthy/control sample. Hormonal/genotype groups are reported but healthy-group whole-brain task effects are presented and described. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI during a social-related task (interpersonal pleasant touch) probing social reward and context (I3); it included a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=24, ages 18–35) analyzed separately (I4); and it reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation results for the control group (e.g., TOUCH > CLOSE and FEMALE > MALE contrasts with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and peak coordinates), satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence (I5/I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of multimodal social communication and empathy using naturalistic video stimuli (task-based fMRI) addressing social communication and perception of others. The sample includes 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.07, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (random-effects GLM; contrasts and peak coordinates described; whole-brain activations shown in figures and supplementary tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This fMRI study investigates neural and behavioral responses to identifying deceptive versus normal soccer moves, which requires perception and inference about others’ intentions—i.e., social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants are healthy adults (three groups, ages 19–33/19–31/19–23), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (experimental conditions vs. non-biological motion) with family-wise error correction and lists peak activations and cluster locations (figures and tables of coordinates), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The study is empirical, not ROI-limited, and not purely connectivity or resting-state. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social/emotional face processing in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2). The task is social-related (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs neutral shapes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses are described; main effects of stimulus type and interaction contrasts are reported and supplemented with tables/figures), with results clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and supplementary tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (Hariri face-matching and social scenes) in a sample of healthy adult participants (N=55, mean age 24.9). The paper reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain activation for the healthy sample (contrast “social > non-social”), including whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reported activation clusters (e.g., bilateral amygdala). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This study includes a healthy adult control group (I4) and uses an fMRI task involving social processing (interpersonal rejection and imagined aggression toward others) satisfying I3. However, the paper reports whole-brain task-related functional connectivity/network results and between-group (BPD vs. healthy) connectivity contrasts but does not present any unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map or healthy-group activation contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. It thus meets exclusion criteria: E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking, attentional reorienting) in healthy adult participants (n=33, ages 20–34), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analyses, searchlight MVPA, GLM contrasts) with reported significant clusters and coordinates (Tables/Figures) clearly from the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are described and thresholded (p<0.05 FWE voxel-level), and results are presented in tables/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
